一.etymology: Cardinal number 'one', written since oracle-bone antiquity with a single horizontal stroke. In spoken Mandarin, 一 undergoes regular tone sandhi: yī in counting and ordinals (第一), rising yí before a fourth tone (一个 yí gè), and falling yì before tones 1, 2, and 3 (一杯 yì bēi).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一 (via 萌典)

一下.etymology: Verbal classifier phrase combining 一 ('one') + 下 ('downward stroke or beat; single occurrence of an action'). Placed after a verb (看一下, 等一下), it softens commands and marks a brief, casual, or single-attempt action.

history.meaning: one stroke/time -> brief verbal measure ('for a moment, once')

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一下 (via 萌典)

一个.etymology: Compound numeral-classifier phrase joining 一 ('one', spoken rising yí before fourth tone) + 个 (default general classifier, originally 箇/個 'bamboo stalk, single unit'). Serves both to count single items and, in colloquial Mandarin, like an indefinite article ('a, a certain').

history.meaning: one unit; a single (item or person)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一个 (via 萌典)

一共.etymology: Adverb meaning 'altogether, in total', formed from 一 ('one single whole') + 共 ('together, shared', attested from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions showing two hands holding an object together).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一共 (via 萌典)

一刻.etymology: Time expression combining 一 ('one') + 刻 ('carved notch on a clepsydra water clock', knife radical 刂 + phonetic 亥 hài). Under the traditional 96-notch daily water-clock system refactored in the early Qing dynasty, one 刻 equaled 15 minutes ('a quarter of an hour'); also used for 'a brief moment'.

history.meaning: one notch-interval on a water clock
quarter of an hour (15 minutes); a short moment

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一刻 (via 萌典)

一半.etymology: Numeral compound of 一 ('one') + 半 ('half', originally an ideogram in bronze and seal script showing an ox 牛 split in two by 八 'divide').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一半 (via 萌典)

一定.etymology: Adverb and adjective meaning 'settled, fixed; certainly, without fail', from 一 ('unified, single') + 定 ('settle, fix', roof 宀 + 正 'upright/foot settled inside a house'). In Classical texts (such as Hanfeizi), 一定 meant 'once fixed or unified'; in Mandarin it grammaticalized into a strong modal adverb ('definitely, must').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一定 (via 萌典)

一干二净.etymology: Four-character idiom built on the numeral frame 一…二… ('first… second… / thoroughly') splitting the compound 干净 ('clean', 干/乾 'dry' + 净 'clean, pure'). Describes something wiped, forgotten, or used up 'completely and utterly clean, without a trace left'.

history.form: 一乾二淨 / 一干二净
history.meaning: thoroughly clean; completely gone without a trace

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一干二净 (via 萌典)

一年年.etymology: Reduplicated temporal phrase of 一 ('one') + 年 ('year, harvest cycle', originally showing a person carrying grain禾) + 年, expressing 'year after year, with each passing year'.

history.meaning: year after year; year by year

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一年年 (via 萌典)

一样.etymology: Adjective and equative marker meaning 'the same, alike', combining 一 ('one and the same') + 样 (樣, 'wooden pattern, model, appearance', tree 木 + 羕).

history.meaning: of one pattern; identical; the same

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一样 (via 萌典)

一模一样.etymology: Four-character emphatic idiom meaning 'completely identical, cast from the very same mold', pairing 一模 ('one mold/matrix', 模 mú 'wooden or clay casting mold') with 一样 ('one pattern/appearance').

history.form: 一模一樣 / 一模一样
history.meaning: from the same mold and pattern -> exactly alike

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一模一样 (via 萌典)

一点.etymology: Quantifier phrase meaning 'a little bit, a touch' (and 'one o'clock'), from 一 ('one') + 点 (點, 'tiny black dot or speck', 黑 'black' + phonetic 占 zhàn).

morphemes.meaning: dot; tiny amount; hour on the clock

history.meaning: one dot/speck -> a little bit; one o'clock

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一点 (via 萌典)

一点点.etymology: Diminutive reduplication of 一点 ('a little bit'), doubling 点 ('dot, speck') to emphasize minute quantity: 'just a tiny bit, ever so slightly'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一点点 (via 萌典)

一直.etymology: Adverb meaning 'straight ahead; continuously; all along', combining 一 ('unbroken, single') + 直 ('straight, unbent', an eye 目 looking straight along a plumb line).

history.meaning: in one straight line; continuously; all along

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一直 (via 萌典)

一瞬间.etymology: Temporal noun meaning 'an instant, the blink of an eye', combining 一 ('one') + 瞬 ('blink, wink of the eye', eye radical 目 + 舜 shùn, from Buddhist translations of Sanskrit kṣaṇa 'instant') + 间 ('interval of space or time').

history.meaning: the space of a single blink -> an instant

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一瞬间 (via 萌典)

一起.etymology: Adverb meaning 'together, in the same place, at once', from 一 ('one') + 起 ('rise, start, batch/group',走 + 己).

history.meaning: in one group/batch -> together; at the same time

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一起 (via 萌典)

一路.etymology: Compound of 一 ('one, the whole') + 路 ('road, journey', foot 足 + phonetic 各 gè), meaning 'all the way along the journey' or 'taking the same route' (as in 一路平安 'have a safe trip all the way').

history.meaning: the whole road/journey; along the way; of the same sort

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一路 (via 萌典)

一边.etymology: Spatial noun ('one side') and correlative conjunction ('at the same time, while…', often paired as 一边…一边…), combining 一 ('one') + 边 (邊, 'edge, margin, side').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 一边 (via 萌典)

七.etymology: Cardinal numeral 'seven'. In Shang oracle-bone and Zhou bronze inscriptions, 七 was written as a cross (+), originally representing a cut (later written 切 qiē) and borrowed phonetically from antiquity for the number seven.

history.meaning: cross-shaped graph borrowed for numeral seven

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 七 (via 萌典)

三.etymology: Cardinal numeral 'three', an ancient indicative graph (指事字) written since Shang oracle bones with three parallel horizontal strokes.

history.meaning: three horizontal strokes = numeral three; repeatedly

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 三 (via 萌典)

三十.etymology: Multiplicative decimal numeral combining 三 ('three') + 十 ('ten') for 'thirty' (historically also contracted into the single graph 卅 sà).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 三十 (via 萌典)

上.etymology: Indicative character (指事字) written in oracle-bone script as a short mark above a horizontal baseline, denoting 'above, top, upper' and verbally 'ascend, go up, board, attend, serve'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 上 (via 萌典)

上去.etymology: Directional verb compound combining 上 ('ascend, move upward') + 去 ('go away from the speaker'), used both as an independent verb ('go up') and as a directional complement after action verbs (走上去 'walk up there').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 上去 (via 萌典)

上周.etymology: Temporal compound of 上 ('previous, preceding', treating time as flowing downward from earlier/above to later/below) + 周 ('week, cycle of seven days').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 上周 (via 萌典)

上方.etymology: Spatial compound of 上 ('upper, above') + 方 ('direction, region, quarter'), referring to the space or area directly above.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 上方 (via 萌典)

上桌.etymology: Verb-object compound of 上 ('ascend, be brought up onto') + 桌 ('table', 卓 + 木), meaning either 'serve food onto the dining table' or 'take one's seat at the table for a meal'.

history.meaning: be served onto the table; sit down at the table

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 上桌 (via 萌典)

上楼.etymology: Verb-object compound of 上 ('go up, ascend') + 楼 (樓, 'multi-story building, upper floor', wood 木 + phonetic 婁 lóu), meaning 'go upstairs'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 上楼 (via 萌典)

上班.etymology: Verb-object compound of 上 ('go to, enter upon') + 班 ('ordered rank, duty shift', originally two pieces of jade 王 separated by a knife 刀, hence 'distribute ranks, standing duty line'). Originally used for court officials or attendants taking their scheduled shift, now the everyday word for 'go to work, start work'.

history.meaning: report for one's scheduled duty shift
go to work; be on duty

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 上班 (via 萌典)

上课.etymology: Verb-object compound of 上 ('attend, go to') + 课 (課, 'assigned lesson, class', speech 言 + phonetic 果 guǒ, originally 'test, assess, assign quota'). Means both 'attend class' (for students) and 'teach/hold class' (for teachers).

history.meaning: begin or attend an assigned lesson/class

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 上课 (via 萌典)

上面.etymology: Locative noun combining 上 ('top, above') + 面 ('face, surface'), meaning 'on top of, above, the upper surface' (and figuratively 'higher authorities').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 上面 (via 萌典)

下.etymology: Indicative character (指事字) written in oracle-bone script as a short mark beneath a horizontal baseline, directly opposite 上: 'below, under, lower' and verbally 'descend, fall, get off, finish (duty/class)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 下 (via 萌典)

下午.etymology: Temporal noun combining 下 ('after, following') + 午 ('noon', the seventh Earthly Branch corresponding to 11 a.m.–1 p.m., midday): 'afternoon'.

morphemes.meaning: following; lower half of the day

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 下午 (via 萌典)

下去.etymology: Directional verb compound of 下 ('descend, move down') + 去 ('go away from the speaker'). Used literally for 'go down' and as an aspectual complement after verbs meaning 'continue on doing' (说下去 'keep on speaking').

history.meaning: go down; continue on into the future

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 下去 (via 萌典)

下周.etymology: Temporal compound of 下 ('next, following', viewing future time as flowing downward) + 周 ('week, seven-day cycle'): 'next week'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 下周 (via 萌典)

下来.etymology: Directional verb compound of 下 ('descend, come down') + 来 ('come toward the speaker'). Used literally ('come down') and as a complement showing an action bringing something to a halt, detachment, or completion up to the present.

history.meaning: come down toward the speaker; settle down

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 下来 (via 萌典)

下楼.etymology: Verb-object compound of 下 ('descend, go down') + 楼 (樓, 'storied building, floor'): 'go downstairs'.

history.meaning: descend from an upper floor; go downstairs

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 下楼 (via 萌典)

下次.etymology: Temporal compound of 下 ('next, following') + 次 ('order, sequence, time/occurrence'): 'next time'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 下次 (via 萌典)

下雨.etymology: Verb-object weather construction of 下 ('fall from above, descend') + 雨 ('rain', a pictograph of raindrops falling from the sky vault): literally 'fall rain' = 'it rains / to rain'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 下雨 (via 萌典)

下面.etymology: Locative noun combining 下 ('below, under') + 面 ('face, surface, side'): 'below, underneath, the lower part, next/following'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 下面 (via 萌典)

不.etymology: General negation adverb ('not, no') for present, future, habitual, and stative predicates, attested from Shang oracle bones through every stage of Chinese. Spoken bù shifts automatically to rising second tone bú immediately before another fourth-tone syllable (不是 bú shì).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 不 (via 萌典)

不好意思.etymology: Colloquial polite formula combining 不好 ('not good, awkward') + 意思 ('thought, feeling, state of mind'), literally 'feel awkward in mind/face'. Originally describing shyness or embarrassment ('feel embarrassed to'), it became a standard everyday expression for 'excuse me, sorry to trouble you'.

history.stage: Qing vernacular (e.g., Hongloumeng) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 不好意思 (via 萌典)

不如.etymology: Classical and modern comparative verb combining 不 ('not') + 如 ('be like, equal, match'), literally 'not match / not be as good as', and by extension 'it would be better to…'.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Analects, Zuozhuan) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: not equal to; inferior to; better to

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 不如 (via 萌典)

不小心.etymology: Negated manner phrase of 不 ('not') + 小心 ('careful, cautious', literally 'make one's heart/mind small and attentive' in Classical Chinese): 'carelessly, accidentally, by mistake'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 不小心 (via 萌典)

不少.etymology: Litotes compound of 不 ('not') + 少 ('few, little'), meaning 'not a few' -> 'quite a lot, many, plenty of'.

history.meaning: not few -> quite a lot, many

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 不少 (via 萌典)

不是.etymology: Negated copula combining 不 ('not', pronounced rising bú by tone sandhi before fourth-tone shì) + 是 ('be; right/this'). Functions as 'is not / no', in rhetorical tag questions, and as a noun meaning 'fault, blame' (赔不是 'apologize for a fault').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 不是 (via 萌典)

不然.etymology: Conjunction combining 不 ('not') + 然 ('so, thus'), literally 'if it is not so' -> 'otherwise, or else'. Attested since Classical Chinese (Mencius, Zuozhuan).

history.meaning: it is not so -> otherwise, if not

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 不然 (via 萌典)

不能.etymology: Negated modal verb combining 不 ('not') + 能 ('be able, can, allowed to'), expressing inability or prohibition ('cannot, must not'). Attested throughout Classical and Modern Chinese.

history.meaning: be unable to; cannot; must not

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 不能 (via 萌典)

不过.etymology: Originally a verb phrase of 不 ('not') + 过 (過, 'surpass, exceed'), meaning 'does not exceed / merely, only'. From late imperial vernacular onward, it also grammaticalized into a mild adversative conjunction ('however, but, though').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 不过 (via 萌典)

不错.etymology: Litotes adjective combining 不 ('not') + 错 (錯, 'wrong, mistaken, bad', originally gold/metal 钅 inlaid in cross-patterns, then 'staggered, mistaken'). Means both 'correct, quite right' and approvingly 'not bad, pretty good'.

history.meaning: not mistaken -> pretty good, quite nice

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 不错 (via 萌典)

专业.etymology: Compound of 专 (專, 'concentrated, specialized, exclusive') + 业 (業, 'occupation, field of study, enterprise'). Used in traditional prose for 'focusing on one's calling' and standardized in modern Chinese for an academic 'major', a specialized 'profession/trade', or the adjective 'professional'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 专业 (via 萌典)

东西.etymology: Everyday noun meaning 'thing, object, stuff', literally 'east and west' (东 'east' + 西 'west'). Emerged during the Tang–Song period—often linked to buying goods from the Eastern and Western Markets (东市, 西市) of imperial capitals like Chang'an, or as a directional merism encompassing 'everything from east to west'. Note that 西 moves to neutral tone (dōngxi) when meaning 'thing'.

history.meaning: commodities from east and west -> things, objects

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 东西 (via 萌典)

丝带.etymology: Compound noun of 丝 (絲, 'silk thread', a pictograph of two twisted skeins of silk) + 带 (帶, 'belt, sash, ribbon', depicting a waistband with hanging cloths): 'silk ribbon, ribbon'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 丝带 (via 萌典)

丢.etymology: Colloquial verb meaning 'lose, misplace; throw, toss; leave behind'. Graphically an ideographic alteration of 去 ('go away, discard') with a top stroke, attested in medieval rhyme books and vernacular drama as a variant associated with 丟/去 ('cast away, lose').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 丢 (via 萌典)

两.etymology: Word for 'two' used before measure words and paired nouns (两个房间 'two rooms', 两把钥匙 'two keys'). In Classical Chinese, 兩 denoted a matched pair (such as two chariot wheels) and a unit of weight, explaining why Mandarin prefers 两 when counting concrete items with classifiers while keeping 二 for abstract counting and ordinals.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 兩 (via 萌典)

严重.etymology: Compound adjective of 严 (嚴, 'strict, stern, urgent') + 重 ('heavy, weighty, grave'). In Classical Chinese (e.g., Shiji, Hanshu), 嚴重 described dignified, stern gravity or strict laws; in modern Mandarin it means 'serious, grave, severe, critical'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 严重 (via 萌典)

个.etymology: Mandarin's default general measure word (classifier) placed between a number or demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个房间). Originally counting stalks of bamboo (written 箇 with the bamboo radical 竹, or 個 with 亻 in Classical texts like Xunzi and Shiji), it broadened by the Six Dynasties and Tang period into a universal classifier.

morphemes.meaning: bamboo stalk / single unit -> general classifier

history.meaning: counter for bamboo shafts, arrows, individual items

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 個 (via 萌典)

个人.etymology: Compound of 个 (個, 'single, individual') + 人 ('person'), meaning 'individual, personal' (as opposed to collective 集体 or public 公共). Widely popularized in late 19th- and early 20th-century modern prose alongside Japanese 個人 (kojin).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 个人 (via 萌典)

个子.etymology: Colloquial noun meaning 'height, stature, build of a person', formed from 个 (個, 'single unit, body frame') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 个子 (via 萌典)

中.etymology: Ancient graph attested on Shang oracle bones—showing a vertical flagpole or tally passing through the center of a drum or ring—meaning 'center, middle, inside, among; China (中国)' (read zhōng) and 'hit the target, be affected by' (read zhòng).

morphemes.meaning: pole through the center = middle, inside

history.meaning: center; middle; inside; hit the mark

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 中 (via 萌典)

中午.etymology: Temporal noun combining 中 ('middle, exact center') + 午 ('noon, the midday Earthly Branch 11 a.m.–1 p.m.'): 'midday, noon'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 中午 (via 萌典)

中央.etymology: Compound noun of 中 ('center, middle') + 央 ('center, midpoint', showing a person 大 standing in the middle of a frame 冂). Attested in the Shijing (Book of Odes: 宛在水中央 'right in the middle of the water') for the physical center, and used in modern Chinese both spatially ('center') and politically ('central authorities').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 中央 (via 萌典)

中间.etymology: Spatial and relational noun combining 中 ('middle, center') + 间 (間, 'space between, interval', originally moonlight 月 shining through double doors 門): 'in the middle, between, among'.

history.meaning: the space in the middle; between

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 中间 (via 萌典)

丰盛.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 丰 (豐, 'abundant, lush', originally a ceremonial vessel 豆 heaped full of jade or grain 丰) + 盛 ('full, flourishing, plentiful', grain mounded in a dish 皿). Describes a lavish, sumptuous meal or rich abundance.

history.meaning: abundant and full; lavish, sumptuous (especially of food)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 丰盛 (via 萌典)

为.etymology: Ancient character (為) whose oracle-bone graph showed a hand leading an elephant (象) to perform work, yielding 'do, make, act as, become' (read wéi) and the benefactive/purposive preposition 'for, for the sake of, because of' (read wèi).

history.meaning: do, make, act as (wéi); for the sake of, because of (wèi)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 为 (via 萌典)

为了.etymology: Purposive preposition meaning 'in order to, for the sake of', formed in vernacular Mandarin by reinforcing the preposition 为 (wèi, 'for') with the completive/emplacing suffix 了 (le).

history.meaning: for the purpose of; in order to

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 为了 (via 萌典)

为什么.etymology: Interrogative adverb meaning 'why?, for what reason?', combining 为 (wèi, 'for, on account of') + 什么 ('what?').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 为什么 (via 萌典)

主人.etymology: Compound of 主 ('host, master, owner', originally a lamp wick flame 丶 rising above a stand 王) + 人 ('person'). Attested in Classical Chinese (Zuozhuan, Mencius) for a host receiving guests or a household head; today means 'host, owner, master'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 主人 (via 萌典)

主管.etymology: Compound verb and noun combining 主 ('preside over, be in charge of') + 管 ('manage, control', originally a bamboo key or pipe): 'be in charge of; person in charge, supervisor, manager'. Attested since Tang–Song administrative usage.

history.meaning: have primary charge of an office
supervisor; manager; be in charge of

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 主管 (via 萌典)

主要.etymology: Adjective meaning 'main, principal, primary, chief', combining 主 ('chief, leading, host') + 要 ('essential, vital, waist/pivot').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 主要 (via 萌典)

久.etymology: Adjective meaning 'for a long time, long-lasting'. Shuowen Jiezi explains the small-seal graph as a person supported or cauterized with moxa from behind (related to 灸 jiǔ 'moxibustion' and 柩 jiù 'coffin kept for a long time'), borrowed since the earliest classics (Shijing, Laozi) for temporal duration.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Shijing, Laozi) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 久 (via 萌典)

之内.etymology: Postpositional phrase combining the Classical attributive particle 之 ('of, ’s') + 内 ('inside, within'): 'within, inside of' (used for both spatial bounds and time limits, e.g. 三天之内 'within three days').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 之内 (via 萌典)

之前.etymology: Temporal and spatial postposition combining 之 (Classical attributive linker) + 前 ('front, before'): 'before, prior to, ago'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 之前 (via 萌典)

之后.etymology: Temporal and spatial postposition combining 之 (Classical attributive linker) + 后 (後, 'behind, after, later'): 'after, afterwards, later on'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 之后 (via 萌典)

之夜.etymology: Literary-styled noun phrase frame combining 之 ('of') + 夜 ('night'), used in titles and event names (e.g., 音乐之夜 'night of music') to mean 'the night of…'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 之夜 (via 萌典)

乐谱.etymology: Compound of 乐 (yuè, 'music', originally depicting strings mounted on a wooden stand 木) + 谱 (pǔ, 'register, chart, notation book', 言 speech/record + 普 'universal/ordered').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 乐谱 (via 萌典)

九.etymology: Cardinal numeral 'nine'. In Shang oracle-bone script, 九 depicted a bent arm or elbow (later written 肘 zhǒu with the flesh radical), borrowed phonetically since the earliest inscriptions for the number nine and symbolically associated in Chinese tradition with ultimate yang and longevity (homophonous with 久 'long-lasting').

history.meaning: bent-arm graph borrowed for numeral nine

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 九 (via 萌典)

也.etymology: In Classical Chinese, 也 was the quintessential sentence-final particle of judgment, identification, and pause ('A, B 也' = 'A is B'). From the Tang–Song vernacular onward, it shifted to a pre-verbal adverb meaning 'also, too, as well, even'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 也 (via 萌典)

也许.etymology: Modal adverb meaning 'perhaps, maybe, probablemente', formed in vernacular Mandarin from 也 ('also, even') + 许 (許, 'allow, grant, perhaps/approximate').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 也许 (via 萌典)

习惯.etymology: Compound verb and noun of 习 (習, 'practice repeatedly', originally showing young birds 羽 practicing flight under the sun/white 白) + 惯 (慣, 'be accustomed to, habit', heart 忄 + 貫 'pierce/string through'). Means 'habit, custom' and 'get used to'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 习惯 (via 萌典)

书.etymology: Originally a verb meaning 'write with a brush' (書, showing a hand holding a writing brush 聿 above 曰/者), then 'written document, letter' in Classical Chinese, and from the Han–Six Dynasties onward the general word for 'book'.

history.meaning: write; calligraphy; written document or letter

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 书 (via 萌典)

书房.etymology: Compound noun of 书 (書, 'books, writing') + 房 ('side room, chamber', door 户 + phonetic 方 fāng), naming a private study or reading room in a house.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 书房 (via 萌典)

书架.etymology: Compound noun of 书 (書, 'books') + 架 ('wooden frame, rack, shelf', 加 + 木): 'bookshelf, bookcase'.

history.meaning: wooden rack for holding books -> bookshelf

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 书架 (via 萌典)

书桌.etymology: Compound noun of 书 (書, 'books, writing') + 桌 ('table'): 'writing desk, study desk'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 书桌 (via 萌典)

买.etymology: Verb meaning 'buy, purchase' (traditional 買, combining a net 罒/网 over cowrie shells 貝 'ancient shell currency', literally 'net/acquire goods with shell money'). Contrast 卖 (賣 = 出 + 買, 'put out for sale, sell').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 买 (via 萌典)

买家.etymology: Compound noun of 买 ('buy') + 家 ('household, specialist/party in a transaction', as in 卖家 'seller', 东家 'proprietor'): 'buyer, purchaser'.

morphemes.meaning: party or person engaged in an activity

history.stage: Song–Ming commercial vernacular to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 买家 (via 萌典)

了.etymology: Neutral-tone aspect and sentence particle le marking a completed action (after a verb) or a newly changed situation (at the end of a sentence). Grammaticalized during the Tang and Song dynasties from the full verb 了 (liǎo, 'finish, complete'), which is already illustrated in its particle sense in Su Shi's Song lyrics.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 了 (via 萌典)

争吵.etymology: Coordinative compound verb and noun of 争 (爭, 'contend, strive', originally two hands pulling on an object in opposite directions) + 吵 ('make a racket, quarrel', mouth 口 + 少): 'quarrel, argue noisily, bicker'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 争吵 (via 萌典)

事.etymology: Noun meaning 'matter, affair, work, job, incident'. In Shang oracle-bone and Zhou bronze inscriptions, 事 (closely related to 史 'scribe/chronicle' and 吏 'official') showed a hand holding a hunting or writing implement/banner at court, denoting 'official duty, service, affair'.

morphemes.meaning: hand holding court standard/implement = affair, business, matter

history.meaning: court service; official affair; matter; serve
matter; affair; thing to do; trouble

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 事 (via 萌典)

二.etymology: Cardinal numeral 'two', written since oracle-bone inscriptions with two parallel horizontal strokes. Used in counting ('one, two, three'), ordinals (第二 'second'), floor/room numbers (二楼 'second floor'), and multi-digit numbers (十二 'twelve', 二十 'twenty').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 二 (via 萌典)

二十八.etymology: Compound numeral of 二 ('two') + 十 ('ten') + 八 ('eight') = 'twenty-eight' (in traditional astronomy, also the number of lunar mansions 二十八宿).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 二十八 (via 萌典)

二十四.etymology: Compound numeral of 二 ('two') + 十 ('ten') + 四 ('four') = 'twenty-four' (culturally familiar from the 24 hours of a day and the 24 solar terms 二十四节气 of the traditional lunisolar calendar).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 二十四 (via 萌典)

二重奏.etymology: Modern musical compound of 二重 ('twofold, double', read èrchóng) + 奏 ('perform music, play an instrument', originally presenting something with both hands at court): 'instrumental duet'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 二重奏 (via 萌典)

五.etymology: Cardinal numeral 'five'. In Shang oracle-bone and Zhou bronze scripts, 五 was written as an X-shaped hourglass between two horizontal strokes (𠄡), representing the crossing of yin and yang or counting marks between heaven and earth.

history.meaning: crossing graph between two strokes = numeral five

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 五 (via 萌典)

五折.etymology: Commercial discount term combining 五 ('five') + 折 ('fold, tenth part retained of the original price'). In Chinese retail pricing, 'N 折' means paying N/10 of the full price—so 五折 means '50% of the price = 50% off, half price'.

history.stage: Late Imperial to Modern commercial Mandarin
history.meaning: five-tenths of the original price = 50% off

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 五折 (via 萌典)

五星级.etymology: Compound modifier of 五 ('five') + 星 ('star') + 级 (級, 'grade, rank, tier', silk 纟 + 及): 'five-star rating/grade' (especially of luxury hotels or service standards).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 五星级 (via 萌典)

五月.etymology: Calendar compound of 五 ('five, fifth') + 月 ('month, moon'): 'May' in the modern Gregorian calendar (and historically the fifth lunar month, home to the Dragon Boat Festival 端午节).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 五月 (via 萌典)

五金.etymology: Compound of 五 ('five') + 金 ('metal'). In Classical Chinese (Wuyue Chunqiu, Hanshu), 五金 denoted the five traditional metals—gold, silver, copper, iron, and tin (金、银、铜、铁、锡); in modern commerce it refers collectively to 'hardware, metal fittings, and tools'.

history.meaning: the five metals (gold, silver, copper, iron, tin)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 五金 (via 萌典)

五金店.etymology: Compound noun combining 五金 ('hardware, metal tools and fittings') + 店 ('shop, store', shelter 广 + 占): 'hardware store'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 五金店 (via 萌典)

交.etymology: Pictograph in oracle-bone and bronze script of a standing person with crossed legs, yielding the core sense 'cross, intersect', and by extension 'exchange, hand over, deliver, pay, make friends with'.

morphemes.meaning: figure with crossed legs = intersect, hand over, exchange

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 交 (via 萌典)

交还.etymology: Compound verb of 交 ('hand over, deliver') + 还 (還, read huán, 'return, give back'): 'hand back, return (something borrowed or held) to its owner'.

history.meaning: hand over and return; give back

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 交还 (via 萌典)

产权.etymology: Legal and economic compound of 产 (產, 'property, estate, production') + 权 (權, 'right, legal title, authority', originally a sliding scale weight): 'property rights, ownership title'.

history.meaning: property ownership; title to real estate or assets

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 产权 (via 萌典)

亮.etymology: Adjective and verb meaning 'bright, shining, clear; resonant (of voice); become light'. Evolved in Han–Medieval script as a graphic variant related to 諒/明 (combining 高 'high' top + 儿/几 'human legs' standing in an open, elevated, well-lit place).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 亮 (via 萌典)

亲手.etymology: Adverbial compound of 亲 (親, 'in person, oneself, close') + 手 ('hand'): 'with one's own hands, personally'. Attested from Tang–Song poetry and prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 亲手 (via 萌典)

人.etymology: Foundational pictograph (象形字) attested from Shang oracle bones onward, showing the side profile of a standing human figure with arm and leg: 'person, human being, people, someone else'.

history.meaning: side profile of a standing human = person, people

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 人 (via 萌典)

人生.etymology: Compound of 人 ('human being') + 生 ('life, lifetime, living'): 'human life, one's lifetime and experience'. Attested since Classical philosophy and Han poetry (e.g., 人生天地间 'human life between heaven and earth').

history.stage: Classical & Han Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 人生 (via 萌典)

什么.etymology: Everyday question word 'what?' (shén me), descended from Tang–Song vernacular 拾沒 / 什麼 ('what thing?'). Used standalone (什么？ 'What?') or directly before a noun (什么茶？ 'What kind of tea?').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 什麼 (via 萌典)

今天.etymology: Noun meaning 'today', combining 今 ('now, present', attested on Shang oracle bones and in the Shijing) with 天 ('day'). Parallels 昨天 ('yesterday') and 明天 ('tomorrow'), and sits before or right after the subject without any preposition.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 今天 (via 萌典)

今晚.etymology: Temporal compound of 今 ('present, current, today') + 晚 ('evening, night'): 'this evening, tonight'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 今晚 (via 萌典)

介意.etymology: Verb-object compound of 介 ('lodge between, let something stick like a thorn or armor plate') + 意 ('mind, thought'): 'take offense, mind, let something bother one' (most often negated: 不介意 'don't mind').

history.stage: Han–Six Dynasties Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: harbor a matter in one's mind -> mind, take offense

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 介意 (via 萌典)

从.etymology: Ideographic character (会意字) showing one person (人) walking directly behind another (人), originally written 从 in oracle-bone script before later adding 彳/止 to form 從 (and simplified back to the ancient form 从). Means 'follow, comply with' and the preposition 'from, since, through'.

morphemes.meaning: one person following another = follow; from

history.meaning: one person following another -> follow; from

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 从 (via 萌典)

从容.etymology: Alliterative binome (双声联绵词, read cóngróng) attested since the Classic of Documents (Shangshu) and Chuci, describing bearing and movement that is 'unhurried, calm, composed, poised, with ample leeway'.

history.meaning: natural, unhurried, and composed in bearing

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 从容 (via 萌典)

从来.etymology: Temporal adverb combining 从 ('from') + 来 ('coming up to the present, hitherto'): 'all along, from the beginning, (with negation) never'. Attested from Tang–Song poetry and vernacular.

history.meaning: from past to present; always; (with 不/没) never

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 从来 (via 萌典)

仔细.etymology: Adjective and adverb meaning 'careful, attentive, meticulous, frugal'. Originally written 子細 in Han–Tang texts (e.g., History of the Northern Dynasties, Du Fu's poetry) with the literal sense 'small and fine-grained', later written 仔細 with the person radical 亻.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 仔细 (via 萌典)

他.etymology: Third-person singular masculine or general pronoun ('he, him'), formed from 亻 ('person') and 也. In Classical Chinese (Mencius, Zhuangzi), 他 (also written 它 or 佗) meant 'other, another person'; during the Tang dynasty it grammaticalized into the general third-person pronoun.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 他 (via 萌典)

他们.etymology: Third-person plural pronoun ('they, them'), formed from 他 ('he / person') plus the plural marker 们 (men). Used for male or mixed groups of people without any subject-versus-object case change.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 他們 (via 萌典)

付.etymology: Ideogram (会意字) attested in oracle-bone and seal script showing a person (亻) and a hand (寸) handing something over: 'hand over, deliver, entrust; pay'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 付 (via 萌典)

付钱.etymology: Verb-object compound of 付 ('hand over, pay') + 钱 (錢, 'coin, money', metal 钅 + 戋): 'pay money, settle the bill'.

history.stage: Song–Ming commercial vernacular to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 付钱 (via 萌典)

以为.etymology: Classical construction 以…為… ('take [something] to be…, regard as…') contracted when the object is omitted or understood into the disyllabic verb 以为 ('think, suppose, assume—often mistakenly').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 以为 (via 萌典)

以前.etymology: Temporal noun and postposition combining 以 (linker marking a boundary in time or space) + 前 ('before, front, earlier'): 'before, previously, in the past'.

history.meaning: prior to a point in time; before; formerly

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 以前 (via 萌典)

以后.etymology: Temporal noun and postposition combining 以 (boundary linker) + 后 (後, 'after, behind, later'): 'after, afterwards, in the future, later on'.

history.meaning: after a point in time; later; in the future

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 以后 (via 萌典)

们.etymology: Plural suffix (們, neutral tone men) attached to personal pronouns (我们, 你们, 他们) and human nouns (朋友们, 孩子们). Emerged in Tang–Song northern vernacular under various phonetic spellings (such as 弭, 伟, 懣, 門) before standardizing on 們 (person 亻 + phonetic 門 mén).

history.meaning: collective plural marker for pronouns and people
plural suffix for pronouns and human nouns

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 们 (via 萌典)

件.etymology: Versatile measure word counting upper-body clothing (一件外套 'a coat'), pieces of luggage (一件行李), and matters or affairs (一件事). Combining 亻 ('person') and 牛 ('ox'), Shuo Wen Jie Zi defines 件 as 'divide, distinguish into distinct items'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 件 (via 萌典)

价钱.etymology: Compound noun of 价 (價, 'value, price', person 亻 + 賈 gǔ 'merchant') + 钱 (錢, 'money, copper cash'): 'price (of goods)'.

history.stage: Tang–Song commercial vernacular to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 价钱 (via 萌典)

任何.etymology: Universal/free-choice determiner meaning 'any, whatever', combining 任 ('allow, let, no matter how') + 何 ('what, which').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 任何 (via 萌典)

份.etymology: Measure word and noun meaning 'portion, share, copy (of a newspaper, contract, or meal)'. Graphically combines person (亻) + 分 ('divide, allot'), created to distinguish the noun/classifier 份 (fèn, 'allotted share') from the verb 分 (fēn, 'divide').

history.meaning: classifier for portions, copies, jobs, gifts

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 份 (via 萌典)

休息.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 休 ('rest, cease', an ideogram of a person 亻 leaning against a tree 木 in the shade) + 息 ('breathe, rest, cease', nose 自 'self/nose' above heart 心). Attested since the Shijing and Zuozhuan.

morphemes.meaning: person resting by a tree = rest

history.meaning: stop in the shade and catch one's breath; rest

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 休息 (via 萌典)

会.etymology: Polysemous verb and noun (會, originally depicting a covered vessel with a lid coming together): 'meet, assemble, meeting' and as a modal verb 'know how to (a learned skill); be likely to, will'.

morphemes.meaning: come together -> meet; master a skill; will

history.meaning: come together; meet; understand; happen to

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 会 (via 萌典)

传.etymology: Phono-semantic character (傳, person 亻 + phonetic 專 zhuān): read chuán as a verb meaning 'pass on, transmit, hand down, spread, summon', and read zhuàn as a noun meaning 'commentary, biography, historical record'.

history.meaning: relay by post-station; pass down; transmit (chuán); commentary/biography (zhuàn)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 传 (via 萌典)

伤.etymology: Verb and noun meaning 'injure, wound, hurt, harm' (傷, person 亻 + 𠂉/昜 yáng phonetic, from 創/𥏼 'arrow/blade wound').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 伤 (via 萌典)

位.etymology: Polite measure word for people—especially guests, teachers, and elders (一位客人 'a guest', 一位老师 'a teacher'). Combining 亻 ('person') and 立 ('stand'), 位 in Classical court texts named a person's proper standing place or seat of honor, naturally becoming a respectful counter.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 位 (via 萌典)

位置.etymology: Compound noun of 位 ('standing place at court, seat, position', person 亻 + 立 'stand') + 置 ('set up, place, position', net 罒 + 直): 'position, location, seat, place'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 位置 (via 萌典)

低.etymology: Adjective and verb meaning 'low (in height, level, pitch, or voice); bow/hang down', formed from person (亻) + 氐 (dī, 'base, bottom, root touching the ground').

history.meaning: low; beneath; droop or bow down

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 低 (via 萌典)

低头.etymology: Verb-object compound of 低 ('lower, bow down') + 头 (頭, 'head'): 'lower one's head, look down' (famously in Li Bai's 举头望明月，低头思故乡) and figuratively 'yield, submit'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 低头 (via 萌典)

住.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining person (亻) + 主 (zhǔ, originally a stationary lamp post). Originally meant 'stop, halt, stay in place', which evolved into both the main verb 'live, reside, stay (at a hotel or home)' and the resultative complement '-zhù' ('hold fast, stop firm', as in 卡住, 记住).

history.meaning: live/reside; stay; resultative complement 'firmly/to a stop'

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 住 (via 萌典)

住满.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 住 ('live, stay, occupy') + 满 (滿, 'full, filled to capacity'): 'be fully occupied, booked solid, filled with residents/guests'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 住满 (via 萌典)

体谅.etymology: Compound verb of 体 (體, 'put oneself in another's body/shoes, empathize with') + 谅 (諒, 'forgive, understand, trust', speech 讠 + 京): 'make allowances for, show understanding and empathy toward'.

history.meaning: empathize with and make allowances for; understand

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 体谅 (via 萌典)

何止.etymology: Rhetorical adverbial compound of 何 ('how, what') + 止 ('stop at, merely, only'): literally 'how does it stop at…?' -> 'far more than, not merely, by no means limited to'. Attested since Classical prose.

history.meaning: how could it stop at -> far more than, not just

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 何止 (via 萌典)

作.etymology: Ancient character attested on oracle bones (originally 乍, showing cuts or work on material, later adding person 亻): 'make, compose, write, act as, regard as, rise'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 作 (via 萌典)

作为.etymology: Classical and modern compound of 作 ('act as, make') + 为 (為, 'be, do, serve as'). Functions both as a preposition/verb meaning 'as, in the capacity of, serve as' and as a noun meaning 'conduct, accomplishment, deed'.

history.meaning: as / in the role of; accomplishment

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 作为 (via 萌典)

作曲家.etymology: Three-morpheme compound of 作 ('create, compose') + 曲 ('melody, musical piece') + specialist suffix 家 ('recognized master or practitioner of an art', originally 'household/school of thought').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 作曲家

你.etymology: Everyday singular second-person pronoun ('you'), combining the person classifier 亻 with 尔 (ěr), which itself served as a second-person pronoun in Classical Chinese. Attested in Northern Dynasties and Tang vernacular texts such as the Book of Zhou (Zhou Shu), 你 gradually replaced 尔 and 汝 as the standard spoken Mandarin pronoun among peers and colleagues.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 你 (via 萌典)

你们.etymology: Second-person plural pronoun ('you all'), combining 你 ('you') with the human plural marker 们 (men). Unlike French vous, Mandarin 你们 always addresses two or more people; polite singular respect uses 您 instead.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 你們 (via 萌典)

你好.etymology: Universal Mandarin greeting ('hello'), built from 你 ('you') + 好 ('good, well'—originally a short wish '[may] you [be] well'). Because two third-tone syllables meet (nǐ + hǎo), the first naturally lifts to second tone in speech: ní hǎo.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 你好 (via 萌典)

保.etymology: Ancient ideogram (会意字) attested on Shang oracle bones showing an adult person (亻) carrying and sheltering a child (子, with swaddling marks in bronze script) on their back: 'protect, guard, keep safe, guarantee'.

history.meaning: adult holding a child -> protect, nurture, keep safe

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保 (via 萌典)

保养.etymology: Coordinative compound verb and noun of 保 ('protect, preserve') + 养 (養, 'nourish, maintain, care for'): originally 'nurture and care for health/people' in Classical Chinese, extended in modern Mandarin to 'maintain, service (machinery, vehicles, or skin)'.

history.meaning: maintain; service; take care of one's health

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保养 (via 萌典)

保密.etymology: Verb-object compound of 保 ('keep, guard') + 密 ('secret, confidential, dense/closed'): 'keep a secret, maintain confidentiality'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保密 (via 萌典)

保护.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 保 ('protect, shelter') + 护 (護, 'guard, defend, shield'). Attested since Han texts and Buddhist translations.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保护 (via 萌典)

保护办.etymology: Abbreviated institutional compound combining 保护 ('protection, conservation', e.g., historic building or environmental protection) + 办 (short for 办公室 'office'): 'Protection/Conservation Office'.

history.meaning: Protection/Conservation Office (short for 保护办公室)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保护办 (via 萌典)

保持.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 保 ('preserve, keep') + 持 ('hold, maintain, grasp in hand', hand 扌 + 寺): 'keep, maintain, preserve (a state, level, or contact)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保持 (via 萌典)

保暖.etymology: Verb-object compound of 保 ('keep, retain') + 暖 ('warmth, warm', sun 日 + 爰): 'keep warm, retain body or room heat'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保暖 (via 萌典)

保温.etymology: Verb-object compound of 保 ('preserve, retain') + 温 ('temperature, warmth'): 'retain heat, keep warm, thermal insulation'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保温 (via 萌典)

保管.etymology: Compound verb and noun of 保 ('safeguard, keep safe') + 管 ('manage, have custody of'): 'take care of, keep in safe custody, storehouse keeper' (and colloquially 'guarantee, for sure').

history.meaning: keep in safe custody; look after; certainly

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保管 (via 萌典)

保证.etymology: Compound verb and noun of 保 ('vouch for, guarantee') + 证 (證, 'testify, verify, proof'): 'guarantee, pledge, assure'.

history.stage: Tang–Song legal/administrative Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保证 (via 萌典)

保险丝.etymology: Modern technical word for an electrical 'fuse': 保险 ('safe, secure', literally 'guard against danger', also 'insurance') + 丝 ('thread, fine wire'). The name describes the device by its job and its form: a thin wire that melts to keep the rest of the circuit safe. A more technical synonym is 熔丝 ('melting wire').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 保险丝 (via 萌典)

信.etymology: Ideogram (会意字) of person (亻) + speech/word (言): originally 'trustworthy speech, truthfulness, believe, trust' in Classical Chinese, then 'envoy/messenger and their token', and from the Six Dynasties–Tang onward the standard noun for 'letter, mail, message'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 信 (via 萌典)

信封.etymology: Compound noun of 信 ('letter') + 封 ('seal, envelope, sealed wrapper', originally planting trees on an earthen mound to mark a boundary, then sealing an official dispatch): 'envelope'.

history.meaning: sealed wrapper for a letter; envelope

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 信封 (via 萌典)

俩.etymology: Colloquial fusion word (合音字, read liǎ) combining person (亻) + 两 (兩, 'two'). Represents a phonological contraction of 两个 (liǎng gè, 'two [people/units]'), so it is never followed by another classifier (我们俩 'the two of us', 兄弟俩 'the two brothers').

history.stage: Qing northern vernacular to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: contraction of 两个 = the two of (them/us); a couple

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 俩 (via 萌典)

修.etymology: Ancient character showing a feather/ornament (彡) and hand action (攵) washing or adorning a person (攸): originally 'adorn, cultivate, make long/orderly', and by extension 'repair, mend, fix, build (roads/bridges), study, trim'.

history.meaning: cultivate; put in order; repair; build

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 修 (via 萌典)

倍.etymology: Classifier and verb meaning 'times, -fold (multiple of a quantity); double', formed from person (亻) + phonetic 咅 (pǒu/bèi). Attested since Mencius and Mozi for multiplying quantities.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 倍 (via 萌典)

倒.etymology: Phono-semantic character of person (亻) + 到 (dào). Read dǎo: 'fall over, topple, collapse, change (trains/shifts)'; read dào: 'invert, turn upside down, pour (tea/water), back up (a vehicle), on the contrary'.

history.meaning: topple, fall (dǎo); invert, pour, move backward, contrarily (dào)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 倒 (via 萌典)

倒车.etymology: Homographic compound with two tonal readings: read dào chē (with 倒 dào 'move in reverse') it means 'back up / reverse a vehicle'; read dǎo chē (with 倒 dǎo 'shift, transfer') it means 'change buses or trains'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 倒车 (via 萌典)

倔.etymology: Adjective meaning 'stubborn, unyielding, blunt in temper' (read juè alone, or jué in 倔强 juéjiàng), formed from person (亻) + 屈 (qū, here paradoxically evoking stiff, unbending temperament).

history.stage: Han–Tang Chinese (倔強) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 倔 (via 萌典)

值得.etymology: Compound verb and adjective of 值 ('be worth, match in value', person 亻 + 直 'straight/equivalent') + 得 ('obtain, deserve, modal marker of worth'): 'be worth (doing or the price), deserve'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 值得 (via 萌典)

做.etymology: Everyday verb for 'do, make, produce, cook, act as'. Emerged in Tang–Song vernacular as a specialized graphic differentiation of 作 (zuò, adding person 亻 to 故 gù) to carry the colloquial spoken reading zuò ('make, do').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 做 (via 萌典)

做梦.etymology: Verb-object compound of 做 ('make, have') + 梦 (夢, 'dream', originally showing a person on a couch/bed 爿 with dim vision 苜 at night 夕): 'dream, have a dream' (and figuratively 'daydream, pipe dream').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 做梦 (via 萌典)

停.etymology: Phono-semantic character of person (亻) + 亭 (tíng, 'roadside pavilion where travelers halt and rest'): 'stop, halt, pause, park (a vehicle)'.

history.meaning: stop at a way-pavilion -> halt, cease, park

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 停 (via 萌典)

停电.etymology: Verb-object compound of 停 ('stop, cut off') + 电 (電, 'electricity, power'): 'have a power outage, the electricity goes out'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 停电 (via 萌典)

偷.etymology: Phono-semantic character of person (亻) + 俞 (yú/tōu). In Classical Chinese (Zuozhuan, Analects), 偷 meant 'remiss, makeshift, snatch a moment'; from the Han–Six Dynasties onward it became the primary verb for 'steal' and adverbially 'secretly, stealthily'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 偷 (via 萌典)

傍晚.etymology: Temporal noun combining 傍 (bàng, 'draw near to, border on', person 亻 + 旁 'side/near') + 晚 ('evening'): 'toward evening, at dusk, nightfall'. Attested in Song poetry and prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 傍晚 (via 萌典)

储藏室.etymology: Three-character compound of 储 (儲, 'store up, save', person 亻 + 诸) + 藏 (cáng, 'store away, hide') + 室 ('room, chamber'): 'storage room, storeroom, pantry'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 储藏室 (via 萌典)

像.etymology: Phono-semantic character of person (亻) + 象 (xiàng, originally the pictograph of an elephant, used in Classical Chinese for 'image, likeness, resemble'). 像 specifies 'portrait, figure, likeness' and the verb/preposition 'resemble, look like, be like, such as'.

history.meaning: resemble; look like; such as; portrait

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 像 (via 萌典)

像样.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective, combining 像 ('resemble, look like') + 样 (樣, 'proper model, standard appearance'): 'up to standard, presentable, decent'.

history.meaning: look like a proper model -> presentable, decent

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 像样 (via 萌典)

兄弟.etymology: Coordinative kinship compound of 兄 ('elder brother', mouth 口 atop a standing person 儿, the eldest who speaks/instructs) + 弟 ('younger brother', originally leather binding wrapped in sequence around a shaft). Means 'older and younger brothers; brothers; fraternal'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Shijing) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 兄弟 (via 萌典)

先.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on Shang oracle bones showing a foot (止/之) advancing ahead of a person (儿): 'go first, earlier, before, first, ancestors/deceased'.

history.meaning: foot stepping ahead of a person = first, before, earlier

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 先 (via 萌典)

先生.etymology: Compound of 先 ('earlier, first') + 生 ('born'). In the Analects and Mencius, 先生 literally meant 'one born before me'—hence 'elder, teacher, master'. In modern Mandarin it remains a respectful title for a 'teacher/scholar' and is the standard polite word for 'Mr., gentleman, sir, husband'.

history.meaning: one born earlier -> elder, master, teacher
Mr.; sir; gentleman; husband; respected teacher

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 先生 (via 萌典)

光.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on Shang oracle bones showing fire (火) blazing atop a kneeling human figure (儿): 'light, radiance, brightness, honor', and by extension 'bare, smooth, used up completely (吃光)' and adverbially 'only, merely'.

history.meaning: fire above a person = light, brightness, glory

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 光 (via 萌典)

光临.etymology: Polite honorific compound of 光 ('radiance, honor with your presence') + 临 (臨, 'look down upon, approach, arrive'). Literally 'your radiant presence descends here', standard in welcoming guests or customers (欢迎光临).

history.stage: Six Dynasties–Tang epistolary Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: honor us with your radiant arrival; welcome

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 光临 (via 萌典)

光秃秃.etymology: ABB-pattern vivid descriptive adjective combining 光 ('bare, stripped smooth') + reduplicated 秃 (禿, 'bald, bare of hair or vegetation', showing grain 禾 over a person 儿 without cover): 'completely bare, bald, leafless, barren'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 光秃秃 (via 萌典)

光线.etymology: Compound noun of 光 ('light') + 线 (線, 'thread, line, ray'): 'ray of light, lighting, illumination'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 光线 (via 萌典)

免费.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective and adverb, combining 免 ('exempt, waive, excuse from') + 费 (費, 'fee, expense, cost'): 'waive the fee -> free of charge, complimentary'.

history.meaning: exempt from fees; free of charge

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 免费 (via 萌典)

全.etymology: Adjective and adverb meaning 'whole, complete, entire; completely, all'. In small-seal script (Shuowen Jiezi), 全 combines 入 ('enter/gather') + 王 (玉 'jade'), denoting 'pure, intact, unblemished jade without flaw' -> 'complete, whole'.

history.meaning: intact unblemished jade -> whole, complete, keep safe

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 全 (via 萌典)

全新.etymology: Modifier-head adjective compound of 全 ('completely, wholly') + 新 ('new, fresh'): 'brand-new, completely new'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 全新 (via 萌典)

全部.etymology: Compound noun and determiner of 全 ('whole, entire') + 部 ('part, section, division, totality'): 'the whole lot, all, entire, complete'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 全部 (via 萌典)

八.etymology: Cardinal numeral 'eight'. In Shang oracle-bone and Zhou bronze scripts, 八 is written with two diverging curved strokes (八) indicating 'part, divide in two' (the ancestor of 分 'divide', which adds a knife 刀), borrowed since earliest antiquity for the number eight.

history.meaning: two diverging strokes ('divide') borrowed for numeral eight

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 八 (via 萌典)

八度.etymology: Musical compound of 八 ('eight') + 度 ('degree, scale step'): 'octave' (the interval spanning eight diatonic scale steps).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 八度 (via 萌典)

公事.etymology: Compound noun of 公 ('public, official, shared', contrasting with 私 'private') + 事 ('business, affair'): 'official business, public duties'. Attested since the Zuozhuan and Analects.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 公事 (via 萌典)

公众.etymology: Compound noun of 公 ('public, general') + 众 (眾, 'multitude, crowd', originally three people 乑 under an eye/sun): 'the public, the general public'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 公众 (via 萌典)

公司.etymology: Compound of 公 ('public, joint') + 司 ('manage, department, office'). First used in Qing dynasty trade for the British East India Company (公班衙 / 公司) and overseas Chinese commercial associations, then standardized across modern Chinese for any 'company, corporation, firm'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 公司 (via 萌典)

公斤.etymology: Metric measure word combining 公 ('international/metric standard', short for 公制) + 斤 ('catty, traditional weight unit'): 'kilogram' (equal to two市斤 'market catties' of 500g each).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 公斤 (via 萌典)

六.etymology: Cardinal numeral 'six'. In Shang oracle-bone script, 六 resembled a peaked roof or tent structure (介/六), borrowed phonetically since earliest antiquity for the number six.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 六 (via 萌典)

关.etymology: Originally depicting a wooden crossbar or bolt drawn across double doors (關 = 門 'double doors' + 𢇇 'draw bolts/threads through'): 'bolt a door, close, shut, turn off (an appliance); mountain pass/customs barrier; concern/involve'.

history.meaning: door bolt; bar a gate; frontier pass; concern
close; shut; turn off; pass; concern

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 关 (via 萌典)

其实.etymology: Disjunctive adverb combining 其 ('its', third-person possessive pronoun in Classical Chinese) + 实 (實, 'reality, substance, fruit/fact', cowrie wealth 貫 under a roof 宀). Literally 'its reality / in fact', used in Classical prose and grammaticalized in Mandarin as 'actually, in fact, as a matter of fact'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 其实 (via 萌典)

再.etymology: Ancient graph showing a frame or structure duplicated/layered a second time: in Classical Chinese 'twice, a second time', and in modern Mandarin the primary adverb for 'again (in the future), once more, further, then'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 再 (via 萌典)

再没.etymology: Emphatic negative phrase combining 再 ('again, ever again, any more') + 没 ('not have, did not'): 'never again, no longer, there is no… anymore'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 再没 (via 萌典)

再见.etymology: Standard Mandarin farewell ('goodbye', literally 'again see / meet again'), pairing 再 ('once more, again') with 见 ('see, meet'). Mirrors friendly 'see you again' expressions worldwide without restricting the time of day.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 再見 (via 萌典)

冒雨.etymology: Verb-object compound of 冒 ('push forward braving cover/obstacle', originally a cap/hood covering the eyes 目) + 雨 ('rain'): 'brave the rain, go out in spite of the rain'. Attested in Han–Tang historical prose and poetry.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 冒雨 (via 萌典)

写.etymology: Originally 寫 (roof 宀 + 舄 xì), meaning in Classical Chinese 'transfer items from one vessel/house to another, pour out, unburden (one's heart), copy a text or portrait'. From the Six Dynasties and Tang period onward, 寫 replaced 書 as the everyday verb for 'write, compose'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 写 (via 萌典)

写完.etymology: Resultative verb compound of 写 ('write') + 完 ('finish, complete'): 'finish writing'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 写完 (via 萌典)

冬天.etymology: Compound noun of 冬 ('winter', the fourth and final season, originally knotted ends of a cord 夂 with ice 冫 below) + 天 ('sky, season, time of year'): 'winter'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 冬天 (via 萌典)

冰.etymology: Noun and verb meaning 'ice; freeze; chill on ice'. In Old Chinese, 'ice' was written 仌 (two chevron-like ice crystals, now the two-dot ice radical 冫), while 冰 (冫 + 水) was a variant of 凝 ('congeal, freeze') before becoming the standard character for 'ice'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 冰 (via 萌典)

冰凉.etymology: Modifier-head adjective compound of 冰 ('ice') + 凉 ('cool, cold'): 'ice-cold,freezing cold to the touch'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 冰凉 (via 萌典)

冰箱.etymology: Compound noun of 冰 ('ice') + 箱 ('chest, box, cabinet', bamboo 竹 + 相). Originally named insulated wooden chests cooled with blocks of natural ice in Ming–Qing households (succeeding ancient bronze/wooden 冰鉴), and was retained in the 20th century for the electric 'refrigerator, fridge'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 冰箱 (via 萌典)

冲.etymology: Merged simplified graph representing two historical characters: (1) 沖 (water 氵 + 中 zhōng, 'surge, pour boiling water over, rinse, infuse tea, rush toward', read chōng) and (2) 衝 (行 + 重, 'thoroughfare, charge ahead, dash; toward/facing [read chòng]').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 冲 (via 萌典)

冷.etymology: Phono-semantic character of ice (冫) + 令 (lìng), attested since Han texts and Шуоwen Jiezi: 'cold, chilly' (and figuratively 'unpopular, deserted, cold in manner').

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 冷 (via 萌典)

冷水.etymology: Modifier-head noun compound of 冷 ('cold') + 水 ('water'): 'cold water, unboiled/unchilled or tap water' (also in 泼冷水 'pour cold water on enthusiasm').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 冷水 (via 萌典)

冷雨.etymology: Modifier-head noun phrase of 冷 ('cold, chilly') + 雨 ('rain'): 'cold rain, chilly rain'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 冷雨 (via 萌典)

准.etymology: Simplified graph merging two Classical characters: (1) 準 (water 氵 + 隼 'falcon' + 十, originally a carpenter's water-level device used to check horizontal flatness, hence 'standard, accurate, exact, definitely', read zhǔn) and (2) 准 (ice 冫 + 隹, an administrative abbreviation of 準 used in official documents for 'approve, grant, allow').

history.form: 準 (water level, standard, accurate) / 准 (official approval)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 准 (via 萌典)

准备.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 准 (準, 'reckon in advance, set as standard') + 备 (備, 'prepare, make ready, equip'): 'prepare, get ready, plan/intend to'. Attested from Song–Yuan administrative and vernacular texts.

history.meaning: make ready in advance; prepare; intend to

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 准备 (via 萌典)

准时.etymology: Compound adjective and adverb of 准 (準, 'exact, accurate') + 时 (時, 'time'): 'on time, punctual'.

history.meaning: exact to the time = punctual, on time

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 准时 (via 萌典)

凉.etymology: Phono-semantic character of water/ice (氵/冫) + 京 (jīng/liáng): 'cool, pleasantly chilly; let something hot cool down; disappointed (心凉)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 凉 (via 萌典)

凉水.etymology: Compound noun of 凉 ('cool, cold') + 水 ('water'): 'cool water, cold (often unboiled) water'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 凉水 (via 萌典)

几.etymology: Simplified character merging two ancient graphs: (1) 幾 (two skeins of silk 丝 guarded by a halberd 戍, 'subtle, nearly, how many?, a few', read jǐ), the source of the interrogative/indefinite numeral 'how many?; several, a few'; and (2) 几 (jī, pictograph of a low small table).

morphemes.meaning: how many; a few (jǐ); small table (jī)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 几 (via 萌典)

出.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on Shang oracle bones showing a foot (止/屮) stepping out of a cave or enclosure (凵): 'go out, come out, exit, produce, issue, happen, exceed'.

history.meaning: foot stepping out of an enclosure = go out, come out, produce
go/come out; issue; occur; directional complement 'out'

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 出 (via 萌典)

出去.etymology: Directional verb compound of 出 ('exit, move out') + 去 ('go away from the speaker'): 'go out' (and as a directional complement after verbs: 走出去 'walk out').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 出去 (via 萌典)

出售.etymology: Verb compound of 出 ('put out, offer') + 售 ('sell', originally a bird/goods leaving the seller's hand through speech 口): 'offer for sale, sell'.

history.stage: Song–Ming commercial Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 出售 (via 萌典)

出来.etymology: Directional verb compound of 出 ('exit, emerge') + 来 ('come toward the speaker'). Used literally ('come out') and as a resultative/directional complement showing emergence, completion, or recognition (看出来 'make out by looking', 想出来 'think up').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 出来 (via 萌典)

出炉.etymology: Verb-object compound of 出 ('come out of') + 炉 (爐, 'oven, furnace, stove'): literally 'come fresh out of the oven/kiln' (of bread, pastries, or metal/porcelain), and figuratively 'be newly released or published (of a report, plan, or list)'.

history.meaning: come fresh out of the furnace/oven; be newly released

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 出炉 (via 萌典)

出租车.etymology: Three-character compound of 出租 ('rent out, lease for hire', 出 'put out' + 租 'rent/tax grain') + 车 ('vehicle, car'): 'taxicab, taxi'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 出租车 (via 萌典)

出门.etymology: Verb-object compound of 出 ('go out of') + 门 (門, 'door, gate, home'): 'go out the door, leave home, travel away from home'. Attested since the Shijing and Classics.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: step out the gate; leave home

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 出门 (via 萌典)

分.etymology: Ancient ideogram (会意字) combining 八 ('part, divide in two') + 刀 ('knife'): 'cut apart, divide, distribute, separate, distinguish' (read fēn), and as a unit 'minute (1/60 of an hour or degree); cent (1/100 of a yuan); point/score; one-tenth'. Read fèn, it means 'allotted share, component, duty'.

history.meaning: knife dividing in two = divide, separate (fēn); allotted share (fèn)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 分 (via 萌典)

分成.etymology: Resultative verb compound of 分 ('divide, split') + 成 ('become, form into'): 'divide into (parts/groups)' (and as a noun/verb phrase, 'share profits by percentage').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 分成 (via 萌典)

分贝.etymology: Hybrid calque-phonetic compound coined for the acoustic unit 'decibel' (dB): 分 ('one-tenth, deci-') + 贝 ('bel', phonetic rendering of Alexander Graham Bell's surname, 贝尔).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 分贝 (via 萌典)

分钟.etymology: Compound time unit of 分 ('minute, 1/60th division') + 钟 (鐘, 'clock, bell'). Added 钟 to disambiguate a 'minute of time' (一分钟) from money cents or test points.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 分钟 (via 萌典)

切.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 七 (qī, originally the graph for cutting) + 刀 ('knife'): read qiē 'cut, slice, chop with a knife (and in geometry, tangent)'; read qiè 'press close together (as in taking the pulse 切脉), urgent, eager, by all means'.

history.meaning: cut/carve with a blade (qiē); press close, earnest, urgent (qiè)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 切 (via 萌典)

列.etymology: Ideographic/phono-semantic character of 歹/歺 ('broken bone/fragments') + 刀 (刂, 'knife'): originally 'split apart, arrange in order', hence 'line up, arrange in a row, list' and the measure word for 'a row, a train of cars (一列火车)'.

history.meaning: divide and arrange in order; rank; row
arrange; list; row; classifier for trains

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 列 (via 萌典)

刚.etymology: Phono-semantic character (剛) of 冈 (岡, gāng phonetic) + 刀 (刂, 'knife/blade'): originally 'hard, strong, unyielding (of metal or character)' in Classical Chinese. From Tang–Song vernacular onward, it developed the temporal adverb sense 'just, barely, just a moment ago'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 刚 (via 萌典)

刚刚.etymology: Reduplication of the adverb 刚 ('just'): used both as a temporal adverb ('just now, a moment ago') and to mean 'barely, just enough'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 刚刚 (via 萌典)

刚才.etymology: Temporal noun combining 刚 ('just') + 才 ('just now, only then'): 'just now, a moment ago' (syntactically a time noun that can precede or follow the subject, unlike the pure adverb 刚).

history.meaning: the moment just past; just now

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 刚才 (via 萌典)

别.etymology: Ideogram (別) showing a knife (刂/刀) separating bone from bone/flesh (咼): 'separate, part, distinguish, other/another (别人); fasten with a pin'. In modern northern Mandarin, 别 (bié) also serves as the prohibitive adverb 'don't!' (widely analyzed as a phonetic fusion of 不要 bú yào).

history.meaning: prohibitive 'don't!' (fusion of 不要); other; leave

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 别 (via 萌典)

别人.etymology: Compound pronoun of 别 ('other, another, separate') + 人 ('person, people'): 'other people, others, someone else'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 别人 (via 萌典)

到.etymology: Phono-semantic character combining 至 ('arrive, reach a destination', showing an arrow hitting the ground) + 刀 (刂, phonetic dào): 'arrive at, reach, go to; up until; thoughtful/thorough (周到)'.

history.meaning: arrive; reach; to/until; resultative complement of attainment

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 到 (via 萌典)

到处.etymology: Spatial adverb combining 到 ('reach, go to') + 处 (處, 'place'): 'everyplace one reaches -> everywhere, all over'. Attested frequently from Tang–Song poetry (e.g., 春眠不觉晓，处处闻啼鸟 / 到处).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 到处 (via 萌典)

到底.etymology: Verb-object phrase of 到 ('reach') + 底 ('bottom, end'). Means literally 'to the very bottom / to the very end' (坚持到底), and as a modal adverb in questions or realizations: 'after all, in the end, on earth (what/why on earth…?)'.

history.meaning: to the very bottom/end; after all; on earth (in questions)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 到底 (via 萌典)

刷.etymology: Character combining 尸/巾 ('cloth/body') + 刀 (刂, 'blade/scraper'): originally 'scrape, wipe clean, brush'. Used in Mandarin as a noun ('brush') and verb ('brush, scrub, paint/coat with a brush, swipe a card'), and read shuā as an onomatopoeia for a swift swishing sound.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 刷 (via 萌典)

刷漆.etymology: Verb-object compound of 刷 ('brush on, apply with a brush') + 漆 ('lacquer, paint', originally sap dripping from a lacquer tree 桼): 'apply paint, brush on paint or lacquer'.

history.meaning: paint with a brush; apply coat of paint

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 刷漆 (via 萌典)

刻.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 亥 (hài/kè phonetic) + 刀 (刂, 'knife, engraving blade'): 'carve, engrave, cut notches; water-clock notch (quarter-hour); moment; harsh/cutting (刻薄)'.

history.meaning: carve with a blade; notch on a water clock
carve; engrave; quarter of an hour; moment

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 刻 (via 萌典)

前.etymology: Originally written 歬 (a foot 止 standing on a boat 舟 moving forward without paddling), later adding a knife 刀 to form 前 (which originally meant 'trim/cut'—subsequently re-written 剪 with a second刀—while 前 took over 'move forward, front, before, ago, former').

morphemes.meaning: foot on a boat advancing forward

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 前 (via 萌典)

前台.etymology: Compound noun of 前 ('front') + 台 ('stage, counter, desk'): originally 'the front of the theater stage' (as opposed to 后台 'backstage'), and in modern hotels, offices, and companies 'the front desk, reception desk'.

history.meaning: front of the stage -> reception desk, front desk

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 前台 (via 萌典)

前面.etymology: Locative noun combining 前 ('front, ahead') + 面 ('face, surface, side'): 'in front, ahead, the front side, preceding'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 前面 (via 萌典)

剩.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 乘 (chéng/shèng phonetic) + 刀 (刂, 'knife dividing'): 'be left over, remain, surplus'. Attested from Tang–Song poetry and vernacular prose (alongside earlier 賸).

history.meaning: be left over; remain as surplus

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 剩 (via 萌典)

剪.etymology: Ideographic/phono-semantic character combining 前 (qián/jiǎn, which already contained a knife 刂 and meant 'trim') + an additional 刀 ('knife/blade') at the bottom: 'cut with scissors, clip, shear, trim; scissors (剪刀)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 剪 (via 萌典)

副.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 畐 (fù/pì phonetic) + 刀 (刂, 'knife splitting'): originally 'split in two, matching counterpart', hence 'assistant, deputy, vice-, secondary' and the measure word for 'a matched pair (glasses, gloves), a set, or a facial expression (一副笑脸)'.

history.meaning: deputy/vice-; classifier for pairs, sets, and expressions

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 副 (via 萌典)

力气.etymology: Compound noun of 力 ('muscular strength, sinew/plow', neutral tone li in this word) + 气 (氣, 'vital breath, energy'): 'physical strength, effort, might'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 力气 (via 萌典)

办事员.etymology: Three-character occupational noun combining 办事 ('handle affairs/official tasks', 办 'manage/do' + 事 'affair') + 员 ('staff member, personnel'): 'office clerk, administrative staff member'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 办事员 (via 萌典)

办公室.etymology: Three-character compound of 办公 ('handle official/company business', 办 'manage' + 公 'public/official affairs') + 室 ('room'): 'office'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 办公室 (via 萌典)

办公楼.etymology: Three-character compound of 办公 ('do office work, handle official business') + 楼 (樓, 'multi-story building'): 'office building'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 办公楼 (via 萌典)

加.etymology: Ideogram (会意字) combining 力 ('strength/plow') + 口 ('mouth/call'): Shuowen Jiezi explains it as adding words or effort one atop another, hence 'add, increase, plus, put in'.

history.meaning: place on top of; add; increase

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 加 (via 萌典)

加倍.etymology: Verb-object compound of 加 ('add, increase') + 倍 ('fold, double'): 'double, redouble, twice as much'. Attested since Han texts.

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 加倍 (via 萌典)

动.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 動, combining 重 zhòng 'heavy/move' + 力 'strength'; simplified 动 uses 云 yún + 力): 'move, stir, act, touch, arouse (feelings), change'.

history.meaning: exert strength to move -> move, stir, act

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 动 (via 萌典)

勺.etymology: Pictograph (象形字) attested from Shang oracle bones and Zhou bronzes showing a curved ladle with a small dot inside representing liquid or food being scooped: 'spoon, ladle' and a traditional small volume measure (1/100 of a 升 liter).

morphemes.meaning: curved bowl and handle of a ladle

history.meaning: ladle with liquid inside = scoop, ladle, spoon

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 勺 (via 萌典)

勺子.etymology: Colloquial noun meaning 'spoon, ladle, scoop', formed from the pictographic root 勺 ('ladle') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 勺子 (via 萌典)

包.etymology: Ancient pictograph/ideogram showing a fetus (巳) enclosed inside a curved womb/wrapping (勹): 'wrap, bundle, pack, surround, include, undertake/guarantee, bag, bun'.

history.meaning: wrap; bag/pack; bun; guarantee; classifier for packs

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 包 (via 萌典)

包装.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 包 ('wrap') + 装 (裝, 'pack, load, outfit'): 'pack, package, wrap; packaging'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 包装 (via 萌典)

区.etymology: Originally 區, showing three mouths/vessels (品) stored inside a curved enclosure (匚): 'store, divide into compartments, distinguish, area, district, region, zone'.

history.meaning: subdivided storage -> distinguish; small area; region

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 区 (via 萌典)

十.etymology: Cardinal numeral 'ten'. In Shang oracle-bone script, 十 was written as a single vertical stroke (|), to which Zhou bronze script added a central dot that thickened into a horizontal cross-stroke (十), symbolizing completeness across all four directions.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 十 (via 萌典)

十二.etymology: Additive decimal numeral combining 十 ('ten') + 二 ('two') = 'twelve' (culturally central as the number of Earthly Branches 十二地支, zodiac animals 十二生肖, and months of the year).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 十二 (via 萌典)

十六.etymology: Additive decimal numeral combining 十 ('ten') + 六 ('six') = 'sixteen' (also the number of liǎng 两 in a traditional Chinese catty 斤, preserved in the idiom 半斤八两 'six of one, half a dozen of the other').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 十六 (via 萌典)

十分.etymology: Degree adverb meaning 'very, extremely, completely, 100%', literally 'ten tenths / ten parts out of ten' (十 'ten' + 分 'tenth part'). Originated in Tang–Song expressions measuring fullness or purity (such as gold fineness or fullness of blossom) on a ten-part scale.

history.meaning: ten parts out of ten (full measure)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 十分 (via 萌典)

千万.etymology: Compound of 千 ('thousand') + 万 (萬, 'ten thousand'): literally 'ten million, countless thousands'. In Tang–Song vernacular it grammaticalized in imperatives and exhortations into an emphatic adverb meaning 'by all means, whatever you do (be sure to / never…)'.

history.meaning: by all means; be sure to

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 千万 (via 萌典)

升.etymology: Pictograph of a scooping ladle holding grain or liquid: originally a dry/liquid volume measure ('liter / pint', about 1 liter in modern metric use), and since the Shijing and Yijing a verb meaning 'rise, ascend, go up, promote in rank'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 升 (via 萌典)
