升职.etymology: Verb-object compound of 升 ('rise, promote') + 职 (職, 'official post, job position'): 'be promoted to a higher job position, get a promotion'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 升职 (via 萌典)

午餐.etymology: Compound noun of 午 ('noon, midday') + 餐 ('meal, eat'): 'lunch, midday meal' (slightly more formal than 午饭).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 午餐 (via 萌典)

午饭.etymology: Everyday compound noun of 午 ('noon, midday') + 饭 (飯, 'cooked grain, meal'): 'lunch'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 午饭 (via 萌典)

半.etymology: Ancient ideogram (会意字) showing 八 ('part, divide in two') above 牛 ('ox'): literally 'split an ox in half', hence 'half, semi-, mid-, incomplete'.

history.meaning: ox divided in two = half; in the middle of

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 半 (via 萌典)

半价.etymology: Modifier-head noun compound of 半 ('half') + 价 (價, 'price'): 'half price (50% off)'.

history.stage: Song–Ming commercial Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 半价 (via 萌典)

半夜.etymology: Temporal compound of 半 ('half, middle of') + 夜 ('night'): 'midnight, the middle of the night'. Attested since Classical prose and Tang poetry.

history.stage: Classical & Tang Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 半夜 (via 萌典)

单子.etymology: Colloquial noun meaning 'printed form, list, bill, slip, receipt; bedsheet', formed from 单 (單, 'single sheet, list, bill') + nominal suffix 子 (-zi).

history.meaning: written list, slip, bill, or sheet

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 单子 (via 萌典)

卖.etymology: Ideographic compound (traditional 賣) placing 出 ('put out, send forth', simplified to 十 at the top) above 買 (买, 'buy, trade with shell money'): literally 'put goods out for purchase' = 'sell' (and by extension 'betray [卖国] or show off').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 卖 (via 萌典)

南方.etymology: Compound directional noun of 南 ('south', an ancient bronze bell/hanging instrument graph borrowed since Shang oracle bones for 'south') + 方 ('direction, region'): 'the south, southern region'. Attested since the Shijing and Mencius.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Shijing, Mencius) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 南方 (via 萌典)

占.etymology: Ancient ideogram (会意字) attested on Shang oracle bones combining 卜 ('divination crack on turtle shell or bone') + 口 ('mouth interpreting the omen'): originally read zhān ('divine, foretell'), and read zhàn (historically also written 佔) for 'occupy, take up (space or time), account for, seize'.

history.meaning: read oracle cracks (zhān); take possession of, occupy (zhàn)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 占 (via 萌典)

卡.etymology: Compound ideogram combining 上 ('up') and 下 ('down') sharing a middle horizontal stroke—literally 'stuck neither able to go up nor down'. Read qiǎ, it means 'wedge, jam, get stuck, checkpoint, clip'; read kǎ, it also serves since the 20th century as a phonetic loan for 'card, calorie, truck (卡车), cassette'.

history.meaning: guardhouse pass; wedge between up and down; get stuck
get stuck, clip (qiǎ); card, truck, calorie (kǎ)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 卡 (via 萌典)

卡住.etymology: Resultative verb compound of 卡 ('wedge, jam between') + 住 ('hold fast, come to a halt'): 'get stuck, jam fast, choke/block'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 卡住 (via 萌典)

卡扣.etymology: Compound noun of 卡 ('clip, wedge, catch') + 扣 ('buckle, button, fasten'): 'snap fastener, buckle clip, latch'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 卡扣 (via 萌典)

卡车.etymology: Early-20th-century hybrid phono-semantic loan combining 卡 (kǎ, phonetic rendering of English 'car' / 'cart') + native head noun 车 ('wheeled vehicle', pictograph of a carriage seen from above).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 卡车

印章.etymology: Coordinative noun compound of 印 ('official seal, stamp', originally a hand 爪 pressing down a kneeling figure 卩) + 章 ('insignia, emblem, seal'): 'seal, signet, stamp'. Attested since Han historical texts.

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 印章 (via 萌典)

却.etymology: Originally written 卻 (combining 谷 'valley/palate' + 卩 'kneeling person'), meaning 'step back, retreat, decline/refuse (推却)'. In Tang–Song poetry and vernacular Mandarin, it grammaticalized into a pre-verbal adversative adverb meaning 'yet, however, but, unexpectedly'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 却 (via 萌典)

卷.etymology: Merged simplified graph representing: (1) 捲 (read juǎn, 'roll up, sweep along, rolled-up item') and 卷 (read juǎn as a classifier for rolls of film, tape, or paper; read juàn as a noun meaning 'scroll, book volume, examination paper', originally from curving the knees 卩).

history.meaning: roll up; classifier for rolls (juǎn); volume, exam paper (juàn)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 卷 (via 萌典)

卷尺.etymology: Compound noun of 卷 (捲, read juǎn, 'roll up, coil') + 尺 ('Chinese foot; ruler/measuring rule'): 'tape measure, retractable measuring tape'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 卷尺 (via 萌典)

卷帘门.etymology: Three-character compound of 卷帘 ('roll-up curtain/shutter', 卷 'roll up' + 帘 'hanging screen/curtain') + 门 ('door'): 'roller shutter door, rolling security gate'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 卷帘门 (via 萌典)

卸.etymology: Ideographic/phono-semantic character combining 午/缹 ('pestle/horse') + 止 ('stop') + 卩 ('kneeling person'): originally 'unharness horses from a chariot and take off armor', hence 'unload (cargo), dismantle/detach (parts), lay down (a burden or office)'.

history.meaning: unharness a chariot; lay off armor

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 卸 (via 萌典)

历史.etymology: Compound of 历 (歷, 'pass through in succession, experience, past ages') + 史 ('court chronicler, historical record'). Used in Classical Chinese for chronicles of past dynasties and standardized in the late 19th century (alongside Japanese 歴史 rekishi) for the modern academic discipline and concept of 'history'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 历史 (via 萌典)

压力.etymology: Compound noun of 压 (壓, 'press down, crush, weigh upon') + 力 ('force'). Coined in modern physics for mechanical/fluid 'pressure' and extended across everyday Mandarin to psychological, work, or social 'stress, pressure'.

history.meaning: physical pressure; mental or social stress

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 压力 (via 萌典)

厚.etymology: Adjective meaning 'thick (opposite of 薄 báo 'thin'); deep, generous, rich (of flavor or kindness)'. In oracle-bone and bronze scripts, 厚 combined 厂 ('cliff overhang') + 石/日 + 子, evoking the massive thickness of earth and rock.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 厚 (via 萌典)

厚厚.etymology: Vivid AA-reduplication of the adjective 厚 ('thick'): 'thick, nice and thick, in a thick layer' (e.g., 厚厚的一本书 'a hefty thick book').

history.meaning: very thick; in a thick layer

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 厚厚 (via 萌典)

原来.etymology: Compound of 原 ('source, origin, original', originally a spring 泉 emerging beneath a cliff 厂) + 来 ('come'). Functions both as an adjective ('original, former') and as an adverb of sudden realization ('so it turns out that…, all along').

history.meaning: originally; former; as it turns out

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 原来 (via 萌典)

厨房.etymology: Compound noun of 厨 (廚, 'kitchen, cookhouse') + 房 ('room, building'): 'kitchen'. Attested since the Six Dynasties and Tang period.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 厨房 (via 萌典)

去.etymology: Ancient graph attested on Shang oracle bones showing a person (大) stepping away from an enclosure or cave (口/凵). In Classical Chinese, 去 meant 'leave, depart from (a place)'; from the Han–Tang period onward, it shifted to the deictic opposite of 来 ('come'): 'go (there), go to; remove/get rid of; past (去年)'.

history.meaning: go (away from speaker); go to; remove

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 去 (via 萌典)

去世.etymology: Euphemistic verb-object compound of 去 ('depart from, leave', preserving the Classical sense of 去) + 世 ('the world, human life'): 'depart from the world -> pass away, die'. Attested since the Jin and Tang dynasties.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 去世 (via 萌典)

又.etymology: Pictograph (象形字) in Shang oracle-bone script of a right hand with three fingers shown. Borrowed from the earliest inscriptions for the adverb 'again, once more (especially of realized or recurring actions), also, both… and…, moreover'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: right-hand graph borrowed for 'again, also, moreover'

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 又 (via 萌典)

双.etymology: Measure word for things that come in natural matched pairs (一双皮鞋 'a pair of leather shoes', 一双手 'a pair of hands'). The traditional graph 雙 shows two birds (隹 + 隹) held in one hand (又)—literally 'a matched pair held together'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 雙 (via 萌典)

双胞胎.etymology: Three-character compound of 双 (雙, 'pair, two', originally two birds 隹 held in one hand 又) + 胞 ('womb, placenta, born of the same parents', flesh 月 + 包 'wrap') + 胎 ('fetus, birth'): 'twins'.

history.meaning: twins born from the same womb/pregnancy

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 双胞胎 (via 萌典)

反应.etymology: Compound verb and noun of 反 ('turn back, return') + 应 (應, 'respond, answer, echo'): 'react, respond; chemical or physiological reaction; response'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 反应 (via 萌典)

发抖.etymology: Verb-object/inchoative compound of 发 (發, 'break out into, manifest a bodily state') + 抖 ('tremble, shiver, shake'): 'tremble, shiver, shake (from cold, fear, or anger)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 发抖 (via 萌典)

发火.etymology: Metaphorical verb-object compound of 发 (發, 'emit, flare up') + 火 ('fire, internal heat/anger' in traditional Chinese medicine and everyday metaphor): 'flare up in anger, lose one's temper; catch fire/ignite'.

history.meaning: flare up; lose one's temper; ignite

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 发火 (via 萌典)

发现.etymology: Compound verb and noun of 发 (發, 'open up, uncover, bring forth') + 现 (現, 'appear, become visible, manifest'): 'discover, find, notice, realize; discovery'.

history.meaning: cause to appear / notice what was hidden -> discover, find

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 发现 (via 萌典)

发车.etymology: Verb-object compound of 发 (發, 'send forth, dispatch, set out') + 车 ('vehicle, train, bus'): '(of a train or bus) depart on schedule; dispatch a vehicle'.

history.meaning: (of a train or bus) depart; dispatch a vehicle

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 发车 (via 萌典)

发软.etymology: Inchoative verb-complement compound of 发 (發, 'grow, turn, feel [of a bodily sensation]') + 软 (軟, 'soft, weak, limp'): 'go limp, feel weak at the knees or in the limbs'.

history.meaning: go limp; feel weak and soft (of legs/body)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 发软 (via 萌典)

叔叔.etymology: Reduplicated kinship noun from 叔 (originally a hand 又 picking up beans/items 尗, used since the Shijing and尔雅 Erya for 'father's younger brother, the third of four brothers 伯仲叔季'). In Mandarin, 叔叔 means 'father's younger brother (uncle)' and is also used politely for any man of one's father's generation.

history.meaning: uncle (father's younger brother); polite address for a man of father's generation

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 叔叔 (via 萌典)

受.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on Shang oracle bones showing one hand (爫/爪) above and another hand (又) below passing a boat-shaped tray or token (舟/冖) between them: 'receive, accept' (contrast 授 shòu 'hand over, give', which later added 扌), and in Mandarin also a passive/experiencer marker ('suffer, endure, be subjected to').

history.meaning: two hands passing an object = receive, accept, endure

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 受 (via 萌典)

受潮.etymology: Verb-object compound of 受 ('be affected by, suffer') + 潮 ('moisture, dampness', originally the rising sea tide): 'become damp, be affected by moisture or humidity'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 受潮 (via 萌典)

变.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character (traditional 變, combining 䜌 luán 'tangled silk threads/speech' + 攵 'hand action' -> 'rearrange threads, change, transform'): 'change, alter, become, turn into'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 变 (via 萌典)

叠.etymology: Character (疊/迭) originally showing multiple sacrificial jade/meat vessels (晶/宜) piled atop one another: 'pile up in layers, repeat, fold (clothes, paper, or bedding)'.

history.meaning: pile up in layers; repeat; fold
fold; pile up; classifier for stacks

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 叠 (via 萌典)

口.etymology: Foundational pictograph (象形字) attested from Shang oracle bones depicting an open mouth: 'mouth, opening, entrance, doorway, spout, cut/nick' and a classifier for family members, wells, bites, or spoken words.

history.meaning: mouth; opening; entrance; classifier for people/bites

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 口 (via 萌典)

口袋.etymology: Compound noun of 口 ('opening, mouth of a bag') + 袋 ('bag, sack, pouch', 代 + 衣 'cloth'): 'bag, sack' and in modern Mandarin especially a garment 'pocket'.

history.meaning: cloth bag or sack; garment pocket

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 口袋 (via 萌典)

句.etymology: Ancient character combining 勹 ('curve, hook') + 口 ('mouth/speech'): originally 'curved/hooked' (later written 勾 gōu) and 'a pause or completed unit in speech/verse', hence 'sentence, clause, line of verse' and the classifier for spoken or written sentences (一句话).

history.meaning: pause marking a phrase; sentence; verse line
sentence; classifier for sentences or remarks

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 句 (via 萌典)

句子.etymology: Compound noun formed from 句 ('sentence, clause') + nominal suffix 子 (-zi): 'grammatical sentence'.

history.stage: Tang–Song literary criticism to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: a verse line or grammatical sentence

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 句子 (via 萌典)

另外.etymology: Compound pronoun, determiner, and conjunction of 另 ('separate, other, another', split from 別) + 外 ('outside, besides, beyond'): 'another, other; in addition, besides, furthermore'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 另外 (via 萌典)

只.etymology: Simplified graph merging two Classical characters: (1) 只/祇/只 (read zhǐ, originally a clause-final particle in the Shijing, then the restrictive adverb 'only, merely, just') and (2) 隻 (read zhī, showing one bird 隹 in a hand 又: 'single one of a pair' -> general classifier for animals, birds, boats, and one of a pair of hands/shoes).

history.form: 只 / 祇 (only, zhǐ) & 隻 (single bird in hand -> classifier, zhī)

history.meaning: only, just (zhǐ); classifier for animals/single items (zhī)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 只 (via 萌典)

只是.etymology: Compound of 只 (zhǐ, 'only, merely') + 是 ('be; focus marker'): means both 'merely is, simply' and as a mild adversative conjunction 'only that, however, except that'.

history.meaning: merely; only; however, it's just that

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 只是 (via 萌典)

只有.etymology: Restrictive verb/conjunction compound of 只 (zhǐ, 'only') + 有 ('have, there is'): 'there is only…' and in correlative conditionals 'only if… (只有…才…)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 只有 (via 萌典)

只要.etymology: Conditional conjunction combining 只 (zhǐ, 'only') + 要 ('need, require'): literally 'only need…' -> 'so long as, provided that' (typically paired with 就 in the main clause: 只要…就…).

history.meaning: only need -> as long as, provided that

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 只要 (via 萌典)

叫.etymology: Phono-semantic character (historically also ) combining 口 ('mouth') + 丩 (jiū, 'intertwine/cry out'): 'cry out, shout, call; animal cry; be called/named (我叫…); ask/order someone to do; passive marker in spoken Mandarin'.

history.meaning: shout; call; be named; make/let; passive marker

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 叫 (via 萌典)

可.etymology: Ancient character combining 口 ('mouth') + 丂 ('exhalation of breath'): originally 'sing/exhale smoothly -> approve, permit, may, can, worthy of (-able)', and in Mandarin also anadversative conjunction ('but, yet', short for 可是) and an emphatic adverb ('really, indeed; in questions: ever/at all?').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 可 (via 萌典)

可以.etymology: Compound modal verb originally formed from two Classical words: 可 ('permissible, possible') + 以 ('by means of, to'). Rebracketed from '可 [以 V]' ('possible [with which to V]') into the disyllabic modal verb 可以 meaning 'can, may, be permitted to; pretty good / passable'.

history.meaning: can; may; be allowed to; not bad

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 可以 (via 萌典)

可怜.etymology: Adjective and verb formed with the Classical prefix 可 ('worthy of, -able') + 怜 (憐, 'pity, feel tenderness or sympathy for', heart 忄 + 粦 lín). In Tang poetry 可怜 often meant 'lovable, endearing' as well as 'pitiful'; in modern Mandarin it means 'pitiful, poor, pathetic; have pity on'.

history.meaning: worthy of pity or affection; touching

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 可怜 (via 萌典)

可惜.etymology: Adjective and verb formed from 可 ('worthy of') + 惜 ('regret, grudge, cherish, begrudge leaving'): 'regrettable, it is a pity, what a shame'. Attested since Han–Tang poetry and prose.

history.meaning: worthy of regret -> what a pity, regrettable

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 可惜 (via 萌典)

可是.etymology: Adversative conjunction combining 可 ('however, yet') + 是 (focus/copular formative): 'but, however, yet' (and when stressed as adverbs, 'indeed, really is').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 可是 (via 萌典)

台灯.etymology: Compound noun of 台 (臺, 'table, desk, platform') + 灯 (燈, 'lamp, light'): 'desk lamp, table lamp'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 台灯 (via 萌典)

台阶.etymology: Compound noun of 台 (臺, 'raised terrace, platform') + 阶 (階, 'steps, stairs leading up to a terrace', mound 阝 + 皆). Means literally 'flight of steps, stairs' and figuratively in 找台阶下 'a face-saving way out of an awkward situation'.

history.meaning: steps leading up a terrace; stairs; face-saving way out

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 台阶 (via 萌典)

右.etymology: Ancient graph attested on Shang oracle bones as 又 (pictograph of a right hand), to which 口 ('mouth', suggesting assistance/eating with the right hand) was later added to distinguish 'right (side/hand)' (右) from the adverb 'again' (又) and 'assist' (佑).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 右 (via 萌典)

右手.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 右 ('right') + 手 ('hand'): 'right hand'. Attested since the Shijing and Classics.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 右手 (via 萌典)

右边.etymology: Locative compound noun of 右 ('right') + 边 (邊, 'side'): 'the right side, to the right'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 右边 (via 萌典)

号.etymology: Originally 號 (combining 号 háo 'cry out' + 虎 'tiger'): read háo 'roar, wail, cry aloud', and read hào 'call, command, name, alias/courtesy title, mark/signal, ordinal number/date of the month, size, brass horn/bugle'.

history.meaning: number; date of month; size; mark; horn

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 号 (via 萌典)

号码.etymology: Compound noun of 号 (號, 'identifying number, designation') + 码 (碼, 'counting tally, numeral symbol', originally agate pebbles used as gaming/counting counters): 'number (phone number, room number, license plate, or clothing size)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 号码 (via 萌典)

司机.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an occupational noun, combining 司 ('take charge of, manage, operate') + 机 (機, 'machine, engine, locomotive'): originally coined in late Qing / early Republican railways for a 'locomotive engineer, engine operator', then generalized to any 'driver, chauffeur'.

history.meaning: person in charge of the engine -> train engineer, vehicle driver

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 司机 (via 萌典)

吃.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 乞 (qǐ). In Classical Chinese, 吃 (read jí) meant 'stammer, stutter' (as in 口吃), while 'eat' was 食 (shí) or 喫 (chī). From the Tang–Song vernacular onward, 吃 was borrowed to write 喫 (chī) and became the universal Mandarin verb for 'eat, take (medicine), absorb, suffer'.

history.meaning: eat was written 食 or 喫

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 吃 (via 萌典)

合.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on Shang oracle bones showing an inverted lid (亼) fitting snugly over the mouth of a vessel (口): 'close, shut, join together, combine, fit, suit, add up to'.

history.meaning: lid fitting a vessel mouth = close, join, match

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 合 (via 萌典)

合同.etymology: Compound of 合 ('join, match together') + 同 ('same, tallying'). In Tang–Song-Yuan commerce and administration, a 合同 was a two-part tally document stamped across the seam so the two halves could be matched together to verify authenticity; today it is the standard word for a legal 'contract, agreement'.

history.meaning: split-tally agreement matched along a seam

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 合同 (via 萌典)

合适.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 合 ('fit, match, conform to') + 适 (適, 'suit, fit, comfortable'): 'suitable, fitting, appropriate, right'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 合适 (via 萌典)

合页.etymology: Visual joinery metaphor combining 合 ('close together, bring two halves flush') + 页 ('flat leaf'), picturing the two flat metal leaves of a butt hinge folding together like the pages of a book around their central pin.

history.meaning: two-leaf metal door or shutter hinge

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 合页

同.etymology: Ancient ideogram showing a cover/frame (冂) fitting over a mouth/opening (口) with a unifying stroke (一): 'join together, share in common, the same, alike' and as a preposition 'with, together with'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 同 (via 萌典)

同一.etymology: Compound determiner and adjective of 同 ('same') + 一 ('one'): 'the very same, one and the same, identical'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 同一 (via 萌典)

同事.etymology: Compound of 同 ('together, shared') + 事 ('serve, work on an affair/post'). In Classical Chinese (e.g., Shangshu, Hanfeizi), 同事 meant 'work together on the same official duty'; in modern Mandarin it is the standard noun for 'colleague, coworker'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 同事 (via 萌典)

同意.etymology: Verb-object/modifier-head compound of 同 ('share the same') + 意 ('thought, mind, opinion'): 'be of the same mind -> agree, consent, approve'. Attested since the Mozi and的后汉书 Book of the Later Han.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Mozi, Hou Hanshu) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: be of one mind; agree; consent

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 同意 (via 萌典)

同时.etymology: Temporal noun, adverb, and conjunction combining 同 ('same') + 时 (時, 'time'): 'at the same time, simultaneously; moreover'. Attested since Classical prose.

history.meaning: at the same time; simultaneously; moreover

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 同时 (via 萌典)

名下.etymology: Locative/legal phrase combining 名 ('name') + 下 ('under'): 'under someone's name (of registered property, accounts, or ownership)'.

history.stage: Tang–Song legal & vernacular Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 名下 (via 萌典)

名单.etymology: Compound noun of 名 ('name') + 单 (單, 'single sheet, list'): 'name list, roster, roll'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 名单 (via 萌典)

名字.etymology: Compound noun originally pairing two distinct Classical naming customs: 名 ('personal given name' bestowed in infancy, from 夕 'dusk' + 口 'mouth calling out one's name in the dark') + 字 ('courtesy name / style name' taken at adulthood). By the Six Dynasties and Tang period, the pair fused into the general everyday word for 'name (of a person or thing)'.

morphemes.meaning: style name -> general word for name (neutral tone)

history.meaning: personal given name (名) and adult style name (字)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 名字 (via 萌典)

后半段.etymology: Three-character compound of 后 (後, 'latter, back') + 半 ('half') + 段 ('section, segment, stretch'): 'the second half, the latter section (of a journey, performance, or text)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 后半段 (via 萌典)

后来.etymology: Temporal noun combining 后 (後, 'after, later') + 来 ('come'): in Classical Chinese 'those who come later (successors)', and from Tang–Song vernacular onward 'afterwards, later on (in the past)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 后来 (via 萌典)

后门.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 后 (後, 'back, rear') + 门 (門, 'door, gate'): literally 'back door, rear entrance' and figuratively (as in 走后门) 'pulling strings, backdoor connections'.

history.meaning: back door; rear gate; backdoor influence

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 后门 (via 萌典)

后面.etymology: Locative compound noun of 后 (後, 'behind, back, rear') + 面 ('face, side, surface'): 'behind, at the back, the rear, later part'.

history.meaning: behind; at the back; the rear

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 后面 (via 萌典)

向.etymology: Pictograph in Shang oracle-bone script of a house (宀) with a north-facing window opening (口): originally 'north window', then 'face toward, turn toward, direction, side with' and the preposition 'toward, to, from'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 向 (via 萌典)

向来.etymology: Temporal adverb combining 向 ('in the past, heretofore') + 来 ('coming up to now'): 'all along, always (up to the present)'. Attested since Six Dynasties and Tang poetry.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 向来 (via 萌典)

向阳.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective, combining 向 ('face toward') + 阳 (陽, 'the sun, sunny south side'): 'facing the sun, sunny, sunward' (famously in the Song verse 近水楼台先得月，向阳花木易为春).

history.stage: Song dynasty poetry to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 向阳 (via 萌典)

吓.etymology: Phono-semantic character (嚇) combining 口 ('mouth') + 赫 (hè, 'fiery red, awe-inspiring', simplified to 下 xià). Read hè in Classical Chinese (Zhuangzi) for an angry threatening shout (as in 恐吓 kǒnghè), and read xià in vernacular Mandarin for 'frighten, scare, startle'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 吓 (via 萌典)

吗.etymology: Sentence-final particle turning any declarative statement into a neutral yes/no question without changing word order. Grammaticalized in Song–Yuan–Ming vernacular from earlier negative finals (such as 无 wú / 么 me appended at the end of a statement to ask 'or not?'), with 口 added to show its purely spoken particle role.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 嗎 (via 萌典)

吧.etymology: Sentence-final particle softening commands into warm invitations ('let's…', 'go ahead and…') or asking for gentle confirmation. Formed with 口 ('mouth') + 巴 (bā phonetic) and evolved from earlier imperative/concessive finals like 罢 (bà, 'finish, let it be') in Ming–Qing colloquial speech.

history.meaning: final particle softening suggestions and assumptions

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 吧 (via 萌典)

听.etymology: Simplified form of 聽 (which combined 耳 'ear' + 壬 + 悳 'attentive heart/virtue': 'listen with ear and heart'). The character 听 originally existed in Classical dictionaries with a different reading (yǐn, 'laugh with open mouth') before being adopted from cursive/popular shorthand for 聽 ('listen, hear, obey, allow; tin can [loan from English tin]').

history.meaning: listen attentively with ear and mind; heed; allow

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 听 (via 萌典)

听听.etymology: Reduplicated verb from 听 ('listen'): 'listen a bit, have a listen, hear someone out' (verb reduplication in Mandarin marks a brief, tentative, or relaxed action).

history.meaning: listen for a moment; have a listen

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 听听 (via 萌典)

听见.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining the action verb 听 ('listen') + the perceptual resultative complement 见 (見, 'perceive, catch'): 'hear (actually perceive the sound)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 听见 (via 萌典)

听说.etymology: Serial verb compound of 听 ('hear') + 说 (說, 'say, speak'): 'hear it said, hear tell, be told that'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 听说 (via 萌典)

听起来.etymology: Evaluative verb-complement construction combining 听 ('listen, hear') + 起来 (inchoative/evaluative directional complement 'when one starts to perceive/judge it'): 'sound (like / adj.), to the ear it seems…'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 听起来 (via 萌典)

吵.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth/voice') + 少 (shǎo/chǎo phonetic): 'noisy, clamorous (of a place or sound); quarrel, argue loudly; disturb with noise'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 吵 (via 萌典)

吵醒.etymology: Resultative verb compound of 吵 ('make noise, disturb with clamor') + 醒 ('wake up'): 'wake someone up by making noise'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 吵醒 (via 萌典)

吹.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on Shang oracle bones combining 口 ('mouth') + 欠 (pictograph of a kneeling person with mouth open exhaling breath): 'blow (with the breath or of the wind), play a wind instrument, boast/brag (吹牛), fall through/break up'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: exhale breath through the mouth = blow; play wind instruments; brag

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 吹 (via 萌典)

呀.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 牙 (yá phonetic). Used both as a sentence-initial interjection of surprise ('ah!, oh!') and as the regular phonetic fusion of the sentence-final particle 啊 (a) after a preceding vowel ending in -a, -e, -i, -o, or -ü.

history.meaning: interjection of surprise (yā); vowel-assimilated form of final particle 啊 (ya)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 呀 (via 萌典)

告诉.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 告 ('report, announce, declare') + 诉 (訴, 'recount, inform, appeal', neutral tone su in this word): 'tell, inform, let someone know'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 告诉 (via 萌典)

呢.etymology: Sentence-final particle used for bounce-back follow-up questions ('And what about X?' 你呢？) and for highlighting an ongoing state ('right now'). Written with 口 ('mouth') plus 尼 (ní phonetic), its conversational particle uses are richly attested in Qing vernacular novels such as Honglou Meng.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 呢 (via 萌典)

周.etymology: Ancient character attested on Shang oracle bones and Zhou bronzes (showing closely planted fields 田 with口, and also merging 週 'go around a full cycle'): 'all around, circumference, complete/thorough, cycle, week; the Zhou Dynasty (c. 1046–256 BCE) and common Chinese surname Zhou'.

history.meaning: closely tended field; Zhou state/dynasty; surname; all around

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 周 (via 萌典)

周末.etymology: Temporal compound of 周 (週, 'week, seven-day cycle') + 末 ('tip of a tree -> end, final part'): 'weekend'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 周末 (via 萌典)

味道.etymology: Compound noun of 味 ('taste, flavor, smell', mouth 口 + 未) + 道 ('way, quality', neutral tone dao in this word): 'taste, flavor (of food/drink); smell, odor, aroma; subtle feel or interest'.

history.meaning: the savor of the Way; flavor

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 味道 (via 萌典)

呼.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 乎 (hū phonetic). Attested since Classical Chinese for 'breathe out, exhale' (opposite of 吸 'inhale'), 'call out, shout', and as a vivid interjection/onomatopoeia for sighing in relief ('phew!') or whistling wind.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 呼 (via 萌典)

呼吸.etymology: Antonymic verb and noun compound pairing 呼 ('exhale, breathe out') + 吸 ('inhale, breathe in'): 'breathe, respiration, breath'. Attested since the Zhuangzi and Huangdi Neijing.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 呼吸 (via 萌典)

命.etymology: Ancient character (in oracle-bone and early bronze script identical with 令 lìng, showing a kneeling figure 卩 beneath an assembly roof 亼 receiving a command, later adding 口 'mouth'): 'command, decree; heaven's mandate; life,vitality; fate, destiny'.

morphemes.meaning: command issued to a kneeling person

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 命 (via 萌典)

和.etymology: Originally 龢 (a panpipe 龠 + grain 禾, 'musical harmony of tuned pipes'), written 和 (mouth 口 + phonetic 禾 hé): in Classical Chinese 'harmonious, gentle, peace', and from the Han–Tang vernacular onward grammaticalized into the primary coordinating conjunction and comitative preposition 'and; with' (also read huó 'knead flour with water', huò 'mix/blend').

history.meaning: musical harmony; peace; gentle; respond in song

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 和 (via 萌典)

和好.etymology: Coordinative verb compound of 和 ('harmonious, at peace') + 好 ('on good terms, friendly'): 'become reconciled, make up after a quarrel, restore good relations'. Attested since Classical histories (Shiji, Hanshu).

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: reconcile; make peace; get back on good terms

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 和好 (via 萌典)

咔嗒.etymology: Disyllabic onomatopoeia (read kāda or kādā) written with the mouth radical 口 on both syllables to imitate a crisp mechanical clicking, snapping, or latching sound ('click, clack').

history.meaning: onomatopoeia for a sharp click, latch, or snap

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 咔嗒 (via 萌典)

咖啡.etymology: Phonetic loanword (transliteration) from European words for 'coffee' (French café / English coffee / Dutch koffie, ultimately from Arabic qahwa via Ottoman Turkish kahve), written with two mouth-radical characters 咖 (kā) + 啡 (fēi) and attested in Chinese since the early 19th century.

morphemes.meaning: transliteration of French café / English coffee

history.stage: 19th-century Qing port cities to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 咖啡 (via 萌典)

咖啡厅.etymology: Hybrid compound combining the loanword 咖啡 ('coffee') + 厅 (廳, 'hall, lounge, parlor'): 'café, coffeehouse, coffee lounge'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 咖啡厅 (via 萌典)

咖啡杯.etymology: Compound noun combining 咖啡 ('coffee') + 杯 ('cup', wood 木 + 不): 'coffee cup, coffee mug'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 咖啡杯 (via 萌典)

咖啡馆.etymology: Compound noun combining 咖啡 ('coffee') + 馆 (館, 'public establishment, house, shop for food/lodging'): 'coffeehouse, café'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 咖啡馆 (via 萌典)

咦.etymology: Exclamatory interjection (read yí with a rising second tone) combining 口 ('mouth') + 夷 (yí phonetic), expressing mild surprise, curiosity, or puzzlement ('eh?, oh?, huh?').

history.meaning: interjection of surprise or questioning ('eh?, huh?')

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 咦 (via 萌典)

咬.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 交 (jiāo/yǎo, 'interlock/cross', referring to upper and lower jaws closing together, replacing earlier Classical 齩 with the tooth radical 齒): 'bite, snap at, grip with the teeth; pronounce words; (of gears) mesh'.

history.stage: Han–Tang Chinese (齩 / 咬) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: bite with the teeth; grip; mesh

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 咬 (via 萌典)

咬合.etymology: Compound verb and noun of 咬 ('bite, grip with teeth') + 合 ('close together, fit snugly'): '(of upper and lower teeth, gears, or latch teeth) mesh, occlude, engage tightly'.

history.meaning: occlusion of teeth; meshing/engagement of gears or latches

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 咬合 (via 萌典)

咸.etymology: Merged simplified graph: in Classical Chinese, 咸 (xián, combining 戌 'axe' + 口 'mouth') meant 'all, completely, together'. Because 鹹 ('salty, salted, briny', combining 鹵 'rock/brine salt' + phonetic 咸 xián) shared the exact sound xián, 咸 was adopted as the simplified character for 'salty, savory'.

history.meaning: brine-salt radical 鹵 + phonetic 咸

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 咸 (via 萌典)

哄.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 共 (gòng/hōng phonetic). Has three tonal readings in Mandarin: hōng ('roar of many voices/laughter', as in 哄堂大笑), hǒng ('coax, soothe a child, wheedle, trick with sweet words'), and hòng ('create an uproar, disperse in commotion').

history.meaning: roar of voices (hōng); coax, soothe, humor (hǒng); commotion (hòng)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哄 (via 萌典)

哆音.etymology: Musical compound combining 哆 (duō, phonetic transcription of the solfège syllable 'do', the tonic first note of the scale) + 音 ('musical note, tone'): 'the note Do (or C)'.

history.meaning: the solfège note Do / C tone

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哆音 (via 萌典)

哇.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 圭 (guī/wā phonetic). Used since Han–Medieval Chinese for the sound of crying or vomiting, and in modern Mandarin as the everyday interjection of amazement or admiration ('wow!, whoa!') and as the sentence-final particle assimilated from 啊 after -u or -ao.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哇 (via 萌典)

哈.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 合 (hé/hā phonetic): 'breathe out with open mouth, yawn (打哈欠), bend over (哈腰)' and the universal onomatopoeia for laughter ('ha!').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哈 (via 萌典)

哈哈.etymology: Reduplicated onomatopoeia from 哈 ('ha'): imitates hearty open-mouthed laughter ('haha!') and functions as a colloquial noun in 打哈哈 ('joke around, laugh something off').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哈哈 (via 萌典)

响.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 響, combining 鄉 xiāng phonetic + 音 'sound'; simplified 响 uses 口 'mouth' + 向 xiàng phonetic): originally 'echo, reverberate' (as in Laozi's 音声相和 and 影响 'shadow and echo'), then 'make a sound, ring, loud, noisy, resonant'.

history.meaning: make a sound; ring; loud; classifier for sounds

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 响 (via 萌典)

响声.etymology: Coordinative noun compound of 响 (響, 'reverberating sound, ring') + 声 (聲, 'sound, noise'): 'sound, noise, report'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 响声 (via 萌典)

哎呀.etymology: Compound interjection combining 哎 (āi) + 呀 (yā), expressing sudden surprise, dismay, pain, wonder, or impatience ('oh dear!, gosh!, oops!, my goodness!').

history.stage: Yuan–Ming drama & vernacular to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: exclamation of surprise, alarm, or dismay ('oh my!, oops!')

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哎呀 (via 萌典)

哎哟.etymology: Compound interjection combining 哎 (āi) + 哟 (yō), expressing sudden physical pain, startlement, or teasing surprise ('ouch!, ow!, oh my!').

history.meaning: exclamation of pain or surprise ('ouch!, oh dear!')

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哎哟 (via 萌典)

哥哥.etymology: Reduplicated kinship noun from 哥 (doubling 可 kě; originally meant 'sing/voice'—the ancestor of 歌 'song'). During the Tang dynasty, northern Chinese adopted 阿哥 / 哥哥 (possibly influenced by or converging with Inner Asian kinship terms like Old Turkic aqa) to replace Classical 兄 as the everyday word for 'elder brother'.

history.meaning: elder brother (replacing Classical 兄 in everyday speech)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哥哥 (via 萌典)

哦.etymology: Phono-semantic interjection combining 口 ('mouth') + 我 (wǒ/ó/ò phonetic). Read ó (rising tone) for questioning surprise or dawning realization ('oh really?, is that so?'), and ò (falling tone) for acknowledgment and understanding ('oh, I see').

history.meaning: interjection of questioning surprise (ó) or realization (ò)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哦 (via 萌典)

哪.etymology: Interrogative determiner ('which?'), written with 口 ('mouth') beside 那 to distinguish rising third-tone nǎ ('which?') from falling fourth-tone nà ('that'). Followed by a measure word (哪个 'which one?', 哪间房 'which room?') or 里/儿 (哪里 / 哪儿 'where?').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哪 (via 萌典)

哪儿.etymology: Spoken northern Mandarin rhotacized (儿化 érhuà) form of 哪里 ('where?'), combining the interrogative root 哪 ('which?') + the retroflex locative suffix 儿 (-r, contracted from 里/儿): 'where?, wherever, anywhere'.

history.stage: Qing Beijing vernacular to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: where? (rhotacized spoken equivalent of 哪里)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哪儿 (via 萌典)

哪里.etymology: Standard question word meaning 'where?', combining 哪 ('which?') and 里 ('inside, place'). Stays in the exact sentence slot of the answer rather than moving to the front: 电脑在哪里？ ('The computer is where?').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哪裡 (via 萌典)

哭.etymology: Ancient ideogram combining two mouths (吅, 'cry out loudly') above 犬 ('dog', originally depicting a hound howling or wailing at ritual mourning): 'weep aloud, cry, sob'. In Classical Chinese 哭 specifically meant 'weep with vocal sound' (as opposed to 泣 'shed silent tears'); in Mandarin it is the general verb for 'cry'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哭 (via 萌典)

哼.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 亨 (hēng phonetic). Read hēng as a verb ('hum a tune softly, groan, snort through the nose') and read哼 (hng) as an interjection of disdain, skepticism, or dissatisfaction ('hmph!,umph!').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 哼 (via 萌典)

商业.etymology: Compound noun of 商 ('trade, commerce, merchant', from the Shang dynasty people who became famous across Zhou China as traveling traders) + 业 (業, 'occupation, industry, sector'): 'commerce, trade, business'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 商业 (via 萌典)

啊.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 阿 (ā phonetic). Serves both as a tone-bearing sentence-initial interjection ('ah!, oh!, what?, huh?') and, in neutral tone (a), as Mandarin's most common sentence-final modal particle softening statements, questions, reminders, and exclamations.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 啊 (via 萌典)

啦.etymology: Sentence-final fusion particle (合音字, read la) combining the perfective/change-of-state particle 了 (le) + the exclamatory/emphatic particle 啊 (a): 'le + a = la', adding lively finality, reassurance, or enumeration.

history.meaning: phonetic contraction of 了 (le) + 啊 (a)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 啦 (via 萌典)

啪.etymology: Phono-semantic onomatopoeia combining 口 ('mouth/sound') + 拍 (pāi, 'slap, clap'): imitates a sharp slapping, snapping, popping, or slamming sound ('smack!, snap!, bang!, pop!').

history.meaning: onomatopoeia for a sharp slap, bang, or snap

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 啪 (via 萌典)

喊.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 咸 (xián/hǎn phonetic): 'shout, cry out, yell, call someone'. Attested from Han–Tang vernacular and histories.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 喊 (via 萌典)

喘.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth/breath') + 耑 (duān/chuǎn phonetic): 'pant, gasp for breath, breathe heavily; asthma (哮喘)'. Attested since the Shijing and medical classics.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese (Shijing, Neijing) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: pant; gasp for breath; breathe rapidly

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 喘 (via 萌典)

喜欢.etymology: Coordinative psychological verb compound of 喜 ('rejoice, delight in', originally a drum 壴 + mouth 口 smiling/singing in celebration) + 欢 (歡, 'joyous, glad', neutral tone huan in this word). In Classical and Tang–Song texts it meant 'feel happy and joyful'; in Mandarin it is the primary transitive verb for 'like, be fond of, love'.

history.meaning: like; be fond of; feel happy

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 喜欢 (via 萌典)

喝.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 口 ('mouth') + 曷 (hé/hē phonetic). In Classical Chinese, 喝 meant 'shout loudly' (still read hè in 喝彩 'cheer') or 'hoarse voice', while 'drink' was 飲 (yǐn). In Ming–Qing vernacular, 喝 (read hē) replaced 飲 as the everyday Mandarin verb for 'drink (water, tea, soup, alcohol)'.

history.meaning: drink (replacing Classical 飲 in spoken Mandarin)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 喝 (via 萌典)

喷泉.etymology: Compound noun of 喷 (噴, 'spurt, gush, spray out', mouth 口 + 賁) + 泉 ('spring of water', originally a pictograph of water flowing out of a cave): 'fountain, gushing spring'.

history.stage: Tang–Song poetry (natural gushing springs) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 喷泉 (via 萌典)

嗡嗡.etymology: Reduplicated onomatopoeia from 嗡 (mouth 口 + 翁 wēng phonetic), imitating a low continuous droning, humming, or buzzing sound (of bees, insects, machinery, or ringing ears).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 嗡嗡 (via 萌典)

嘛.etymology: Sentence-final modal particle (neutral tone ma) combining 口 ('mouth') + 麻 (má phonetic). Marks a point as obvious, reasonable, or something the listener should already know ('well, of course, after all'), or marks a topic pause.

history.meaning: modal particle indicating obviousness ('well, naturally') or topic pause

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 嘛 (via 萌典)

嘴硬.etymology: Subject-predicate idiom used as an adjective/verb, combining 嘴 ('mouth, speech') + 硬 ('hard, stiff, unyielding'): 'stubborn in speech, refusing to admit fault or defeat verbally even when inwardly wrong or scared'.

history.meaning: talk tough; refuse to admit fault or weakness

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 嘴硬 (via 萌典)

噪音.etymology: Compound noun of 噪 ('chirping of a flock of birds in a tree -> clamor, din, harsh noise', 口 + 喿) + 音 ('sound'): 'noise, unwanted or grating sound, acoustic noise'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 噪音 (via 萌典)

四.etymology: Cardinal numeral 'four'. Originally written in early Shang oracle-bone script with four horizontal strokes (亖), then replaced by the borrowed graph 四 (originally a pictograph of the nose/nostrils exhaling breath, later written 泗 'nasal mucus' and 呬 'breathe').

history.meaning: four horizontal strokes replaced by borrowed graph 四 = numeral four

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 四 (via 萌典)

四十.etymology: Multiplicative decimal numeral of 四 ('four') + 十 ('ten') = 'forty' (historically also written with the single contracted character 卌 xì, and famous from Confucius's 吾十有五而志于学…四十而不惑 'at forty I had no doubts').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 四十 (via 萌典)

回.etymology: Ancient pictograph/ideogram attested in oracle-bone and bronze scripts as a spiral whirlpool or eddy (回): 'revolve, turn around -> return, go/come back, reply/answer, chapter/time (classifier for occurrences or chapters of vernacular novels)'.

morphemes.meaning: revolving spiral = turn back, return, reply

history.meaning: return; go back; reply; classifier for times/chapters

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 回 (via 萌典)

回声.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 回 ('return, rebound') + 声 (聲, 'sound, voice'): 'reflected sound, echo'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 回声 (via 萌典)

回头.etymology: Verb-object compound of 回 ('turn back') + 头 (頭, 'head'). Means literally 'turn one's head around / look back', figuratively 'repent/turn back', and in colloquial northern Mandarin an adverb meaning 'in a little while, later on (回头见 see you later)'.

history.meaning: turn one's head back; later on / shortly

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 回头 (via 萌典)

回家.etymology: Verb-object compound of 回 ('return, go back to') + 家 ('home, family'): 'return home, go home'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 回家 (via 萌典)

回形针.etymology: Three-character descriptive compound of 回形 ('shaped like the nested rectangular character 回') + 针 (針, 'pin, needle, wire clip'): 'paper clip' (named after the looped concentric rectangle shape of a Gem paper clip).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 回形针 (via 萌典)

回忆.etymology: Compound verb and noun of 回 ('turn back toward the past') + 忆 (憶, 'remember, call to mind', heart 忄 + 意): 'recall, recollect, reminisce; memory, recollection'.

history.meaning: call past events back to mind; recollection; memory

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 回忆 (via 萌典)

回来.etymology: Directional verb compound of 回 ('return') + 来 ('come toward the speaker'): 'come back, return here' (and as a directional complement after verbs: 拿回来 'bring back').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 回来 (via 萌典)

因为.etymology: Causal conjunction and preposition combining 因 ('rely on, follow upon, because of') + 为 (為, read wèi, 'for the sake of, because of'): 'because, on account of, owing to' (often paired with 所以 'therefore').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 因为 (via 萌典)

围.etymology: Originally 圍, showing an enclosure (囗) around 韋 (wéi, which in oracle-bone script depicted feet walking in a circle around a walled town): 'surround, enclose, encircle, gather around; circumference; scarf/apron'.

history.meaning: patrol around a walled town = surround, besiege, enclose

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 围 (via 萌典)

图.etymology: Originally 圖 (an enclosure 囗 containing 啚 bǐ, 'granary/village boundaries'): originally 'map out territory and granaries', hence 'drawing, map, chart, diagram, picture; plan, seek, scheme for'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 图 (via 萌典)

图书馆.etymology: Three-character compound of 图书 ('charts and books -> books and publications', recalling the Classical pair 河图洛书) + 馆 (館, 'public building, hall, institution'): 'library'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 图书馆 (via 萌典)

图纸.etymology: Compound noun of 图 (圖, 'technical drawing, blueprint, plan') + 纸 (紙, 'paper'): 'architectural or engineering drawing, blueprint, plan'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 图纸 (via 萌典)

圆.etymology: Phono-semantic character (圓) combining 囗 ('enclosure, circle') + 员 (員, yuán, originally depicting a round bronze cauldron mouth 口 above 鼎): 'round, circular, spherical; full (of the moon); make complete/plausible; unit of currency (yuan)'.

history.meaning: round cauldron rim -> circular, round, complete

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 圆 (via 萌典)

圆圆.etymology: Vivid AA-reduplication of the adjective 圆 ('round'): 'nice and round, perfectly round' (e.g., 圆圆的月亮 'the round full moon').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 圆圆 (via 萌典)

圆舞曲.etymology: Semantic calque coined for the European waltz: 圆 ('round/revolving') + 舞 ('dance') + 曲 ('musical piece'), literally 'revolving-dance music', capturing the whirling turns behind German Walzer (from walzen 'revolve').

cognates.meaning: revolving ballroom dance in 3/4 time (semantic model)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 圆舞曲 (via 萌典)

圈.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 囗 ('enclosure') + 卷 (juàn/quān phonetic). Originally read juàn for an 'animal pen or fold'; read quān as a noun, classifier, and verb meaning 'circle, ring, loop; classifier for laps or rounds; enclose or mark with a circle'.

history.meaning: circle; ring; loop; classifier for laps or rounds

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 圈 (via 萌典)

在.etymology: Locative verb ('be at, in, on'), locative coverb ('at, in'), and progressive marker ('right in the middle of doing'). In Classical Chinese (Analects, Shijing), 在 already means 'reside in, be located at, exist'; modern Mandarin extends that 'being at a point' sense to ongoing actions before verbs.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 在 (via 萌典)

地.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 土 ('earth, soil, ground') + 也 (yě/dì phonetic). Read dì as a noun meaning 'the earth (paired with 天 heaven), ground, land, floor, place, position'; read neutral-tone de in Mandarin as the structural particle turning an adjective or phrase into a pre-verbal adverbial modifier (慢慢地走).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 地 (via 萌典)

地上.etymology: Locative compound combining 地 ('ground, floor') + 上 ('on, surface'): 'on the ground, on the floor'.

history.meaning: on the ground; on the floor; on earth

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 地上 (via 萌典)

地下室.etymology: Three-character compound of 地下 ('underground, below ground level') + 室 ('room, chamber'): 'basement, cellar'.

history.meaning: room below ground level; basement; cellar

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 地下室 (via 萌典)

地址.etymology: Compound noun of 地 ('land, place, location') + 址 ('foundation of a wall or building, site', earth 土 + 止 'foot/base'): originally 'land site, plot foundation' in Tang–Song texts, and in modern Mandarin the standard word for a mailing or street 'address'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 地址 (via 萌典)

地方.etymology: Compound of 地 ('earth, land') + 方 ('square, region, quarter'). Originated in ancient Chinese cosmology (天圆地方 'heaven is round and earth is square/quartered'), evolved into 'local region/administration (di fang)' vs. the central court, and with neutral tone (dìfang) became the everyday noun for 'place, space, spot, part'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 地方 (via 萌典)

地板.etymology: Compound noun of 地 ('ground, floor') + 板 ('wooden plank, board'): 'wooden floorboards, floor (of an indoor room)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 地板 (via 萌典)

地毯.etymology: Compound noun of 地 ('floor, ground') + 毯 ('woven woolen rug or blanket', hair/wool 毛 + 炎): 'carpet, rug'. Attested since Tang–Song accounts of Central Asian and domestic woven rugs.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 地毯 (via 萌典)

场.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 場, earth 土 + 易 yáng): originally 'cleared, packed flat earth used for sacrifices or threshing grain', hence 'open ground, square, stage, field, scene' and a verbal/nominal classifier for 'a bout, session, show, match, or spell of rain (一场雨)'.

history.meaning: site; field; venue; classifier for events, shows, or rain

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 场 (via 萌典)

坏.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 壞, combining earth 土 + 褱 huái; simplified 坏 uses 土 + 不): in Classical Chinese 'crumble, collapse (of earthen walls or buildings), ruin, spoil', and in modern Mandarin the general adjective and complement for 'broken, out of order, spoiled, bad, wicked'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 坏 (via 萌典)

坏了.etymology: Predicative and exclamatory phrase combining 坏 ('broken, spoiled, gone wrong') + change-of-state particle 了 (le): '(something) is broken / out of order / spoiled' and as an exclamation 'uh-oh!, oh no!'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 坏了 (via 萌典)

坐.etymology: Ancient ideogram (会意字) showing two people (从) kneeling/sitting facing each other on the ground/earth (土): 'sit, take a seat; travel by (bus, train, plane, boat); (of buildings) face a direction; put a pot on the stove'.

history.meaning: two figures kneeling on the ground = sit

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 坐 (via 萌典)

坑.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 土 ('earth, ground') + 亢 (kāng, 'neck/high hollow'): 'pit, hole, hollow in the ground, depression, tunnel' (and colloquially 'entrap, cheat').

history.stage: Classical Chinese (originally 阬 / 坑) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 坑 (via 萌典)

块.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 塊, earth 土 + 鬼 guǐ; simplified 块 uses 土 + 夬 guài): originally 'clod or lump of earth' in Classical Chinese (Zhuangzi, Chuci). In Mandarin it became the standard classifier for 'a piece, lump, chunk, slice, plot of land' and for the basic unit of currency ('yuan, buck', 一块钱).

history.meaning: classifier for pieces, chunks, and currency units (yuan)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 块 (via 萌典)

垃圾桶.etymology: Three-character compound of 垃圾 ('rubbish, trash, garbage', originally a southern/Wu dialect compound 垃圾 lèsè adopted into standard Mandarin as lājī) + 桶 ('bucket, pail, bin', wood 木 + 甬): 'trash can, wastebin, garbage bin'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 垃圾桶 (via 萌典)

城区.etymology: Compound noun of 城 ('walled city, urban center') + 区 (區, 'district, area, zone'): 'urban area, city proper, city district'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 城区 (via 萌典)

城外.etymology: Locative compound of 城 ('city wall, city') + 外 ('outside'): 'outside the city walls, on the outskirts of town'. Attested throughout Classical and Tang–Song poetry.

history.stage: Classical & Tang–Song Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 城外 (via 萌典)

城市.etymology: Coordinative noun compound pairing the two defining institutions of traditional Chinese urban settlements: 城 ('rammed-earth defensive city wall and administrative seat', 土 + 成) + 市 ('enclosed marketplace for trade'). Together they form the modern word for 'city, town'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 城市 (via 萌典)

城里.etymology: Locative compound of 城 ('city') + 里 (裡, 'inside'): 'inside the city, in town, downtown'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 城里 (via 萌典)

堵.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 土 ('earth, rammed-earth wall') + 者 (zhě/dǔ phonetic). In Classical Chinese, 堵 meant 'a section of earthen wall (and classifier for walls: 一堵墙)'; from the medieval period onward it also became a verb meaning 'stop up, block, clog, feel stifled'.

history.meaning: block up; clog; congested; classifier for walls

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 堵 (via 萌典)

堵车.etymology: Verb-object compound of 堵 ('block, congest') + 车 ('vehicles, traffic'): 'have a traffic jam, be stuck in traffic'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 堵车 (via 萌典)

塞.etymology: Ancient character showing two hands (廾) placing bricks/blocks (𡨄) in a gap with earth (土) at the bottom: read sāi in everyday Mandarin for 'stuff, cram, plug up, cork, stopper'; read sài for 'frontier pass/fortress (边塞)'; read sè in formal compounds like 堵塞 ('block, obstruct').

morphemes.meaning: hands packing blocks into a space

history.meaning: fill a gap; block up; frontier stronghold
stuff, plug, stopper (sāi); block (sè); frontier pass (sài)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 塞 (via 萌典)

墙.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 牆, originally combining 爿 'planks/framing boards for rammed earth' + 嗇 sè/qiáng phonetic, later written with the earth radical 土): 'wall (of a room, house, or courtyard)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 墙 (via 萌典)

墙上.etymology: Locative compound combining 墙 ('wall') + 上 ('on, upon'): 'on the wall'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 墙上 (via 萌典)

墙边.etymology: Locative compound combining 墙 ('wall') + 边 (邊, 'side, edge'): 'by the wall, alongside the wall'.

history.meaning: beside the wall; along the wall

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 墙边 (via 萌典)

墨水.etymology: Compound of 墨 ('black soot ink', combining 黑 'black' + 土 'earth', from pine-soot inksticks) + 水 ('water/liquid'), naming liquid pen ink in contrast to solid inksticks ground on an inkstone.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 墨水 (via 萌典)

声.etymology: Ancient character (traditional 聲) showing a hand with a mallet (殳) striking a suspended L-shaped stone chime (聲/磬) and an ear (耳) listening below: 'sound, voice, tone (the four tones of Mandarin 四声); make a sound; reputation; classifier for utterances or sounds'.

morphemes.meaning: stone chime + mallet + ear = sound, voice

history.meaning: striking a stone chime heard by the ear = sound, voice, tone
sound; voice; tone; classifier for sounds

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 声 (via 萌典)

声学.etymology: Compound academic noun combining 声 (聲, 'sound') + 学 (學, 'study, science, -logy'): 'acoustics'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 声学 (via 萌典)

声音.etymology: Coordinative noun compound pairing two Classical acoustic terms: 声 (聲, 'general sound or vocal sound') + 音 ('articulated musical tone or speech sound'). In modern Mandarin they fuse into the everyday word for 'sound, voice'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 声音 (via 萌典)

壶.etymology: Pictograph (traditional 壺) attested from Shang oracle bones and Zhou bronzes depicting a round-bellied bronze or ceramic vessel with a lid (士) on top and a ring foot at the bottom: 'pot, kettle, teapot, flask, jug' and classifier for pots of liquid.

morphemes.meaning: body and foot of a pot

history.meaning: lidded ritual wine or water vessel
kettle; teapot; flask; classifier for pots

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 壶 (via 萌典)

壶嘴.etymology: Compound noun of 壶 (壺, 'kettle, teapot') + 嘴 ('beak, mouth, spout'): 'spout of a kettle or teapot'.

history.meaning: spout of a teapot or kettle

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 壶嘴 (via 萌典)

备注.etymology: Compound noun and verb of 备 (備, 'prepare for reference') + 注 ('explanatory note, annotation'): 'remark, note, comment field (on a form, order, or document)'.

history.meaning: explanatory note or remark for reference

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 备注 (via 萌典)

备用.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective and verb, combining 备 (備, 'prepare in advance, keep in reserve') + 用 ('use'): 'keep in reserve for future or emergency use; spare, backup (e.g., 备用钥匙 spare key)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 备用 (via 萌典)

夏天.etymology: Compound noun of 夏 ('summer', originally a grand human figure with head 页, hands, and feet 夊 in ceremonial dance, denoting the great flourishing season) + 天 ('season, sky, time of year'): 'summer'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 夏天 (via 萌典)

外.etymology: Ideogram combining 夕 ('evening/crescent moon') + 卜 ('divination crack'): Shuowen Jiezi notes that divining was normally performed by day, so divining at night (夕) was 'outside the norm / beyond', yielding the core spatial sense 'outside, exterior, outer, foreign, other, maternal relatives'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 外 (via 萌典)

外头.etymology: Colloquial locative noun combining 外 ('outside') + nominal locative suffix 头 (頭, neutral tone tou, bleached from 'head/end'): 'outside, outdoors'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 外头 (via 萌典)

外套.etymology: Compound noun of 外 ('outer') + 套 ('outer case, cover, garment worn over others'): 'outer coat, jacket, overcoat'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 外套 (via 萌典)

外皮.etymology: Compound noun of 外 ('outer, exterior') + 皮 ('skin, peel, bark, rind, cover'): 'outer skin, peel, rind, outer casing or wrapper'.

history.meaning: outer skin, bark, peel, or cover

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 外皮 (via 萌典)

外面.etymology: Locative compound noun of 外 ('outside, exterior') + 面 ('face, surface, side'): 'outside, outdoors, the exterior surface'.

history.stage: Classical & Vernacular Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 外面 (via 萌典)

多.etymology: Ideogram (会意字) attested on Shang oracle bones doubling 夕 (originally depicting two pieces of meat 肉/夕 stacked one atop another): 'many, much, plenty, more (opposite of 少 'few/little'); how…! (in exclamations and degree questions like 多大); odd/over (after round numbers: 十多个)'.

history.meaning: doubled pieces of meat = many, much, abundant

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 多 (via 萌典)

多亏.etymology: Adverb and verb compound of 多 ('greatly, much') + 亏 (虧, 'owe to, thanks to someone's effort/favor'): 'thanks to, luckily because of'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 多亏 (via 萌典)

多半.etymology: Compound quantifier and epistemic adverb of 多 ('more than') + 半 ('half'): 'more than half, the majority; most likely, probably'. Attested from Tang–Song poetry.

history.meaning: more than half; most likely, probably

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 多半 (via 萌典)

多少.etymology: Antonymic compound combining 多 ('many, much') + 少 ('few, little', neutral tone shao when asking quantity): originally a Classical abstract noun meaning 'relative quantity (how much or how little)', which evolved into the standard interrogative numeral 'how many?, how much?' and indefinite 'somewhat, to some extent'.

history.meaning: how many?; how much?; more or less

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 多少 (via 萌典)

夜.etymology: Phono-semantic/ideographic character attested in bronze script combining 夕 ('crescent moon, dusk') + 亦 (yì phonetic, originally a standing person with dots under the arms): 'night, nighttime, darkness'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 夜 (via 萌典)

夜空.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 夜 ('night') + 空 ('sky, air'): 'the night sky'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 夜空 (via 萌典)

够到.etymology: Resultative verb compound combining 够 (夠, 'reach by stretching out the hand or body') + 到 ('attain, reach'): 'reach (an object high up or far away)'.

history.meaning: reach by stretching; get hold of

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 够到 (via 萌典)

大.etymology: Foundational pictograph (象形字) attested from Shang oracle bones showing a front-facing human figure standing with arms and legs stretched wide: 'big, large, great, wide, loud, strong, eldest, adult, very'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: person standing with arms and legs spread = big, great, large

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大 (via 萌典)

大厅.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 大 ('large, main') + 厅 (廳, 'hall, reception room'): 'main hall, lobby, concourse, grand hall'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大厅 (via 萌典)

大哥.etymology: Compound kinship and social title of 大 ('eldest') + 哥 ('elder brother'): 'eldest brother' (and used respectfully or colloquially to address an older man or friend of one's own generation).

history.meaning: eldest brother; friendly/respectful address for an older man

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大哥 (via 萌典)

大堂.etymology: Compound noun of 大 ('main, grand') + 堂 ('elevated main hall of a palace, yamen court, or residence'). Historically the central courtroom of a magistrate's yamen or the main hall of a mansion; in modern Mandarin, the 'main lobby' of a hotel, bank, or commercial building.

history.meaning: main hall of a residence or magistrate's court
hotel or bank lobby; main hall

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大堂 (via 萌典)

大家.etymology: Compound of 大 ('great, all') + 家 ('household, clan, people'). In Classical Chinese (Zuozhuan, Mencius), 大家 meant 'a great noble clan or household' (or a great master); from the Six Dynasties and Tang–Song vernacular onward, it grammaticalized into the inclusive collective pronoun 'everyone, everybody, all of us'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大家 (via 萌典)

大山.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 大 ('big, great, high') + 山 ('mountain'): 'large mountain, high mountains, mountain range'.

history.stage: Old & Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大山 (via 萌典)

大师.etymology: Compound noun of 大 ('great') + 师 (師, 'master, teacher'). Used in Classical and Buddhist texts for a revered spiritual teacher or monk, and in modern Mandarin for a 'grandmaster, great master (of art, music, craft, or scholarship)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大师 (via 萌典)

大方.etymology: Compound of 大 ('great') + 方 ('method/principle; square earth'). In Classical Chinese (Zhuangzi's 吾长见笑于大方之家), 大方 meant 'great principles / experts of great learning'. In vernacular Mandarin (read dàfang with neutral tone), it means 'generous, ungrudging with money; natural, poised, and tasteful in manner or design'.

history.meaning: generous; poised and natural; in good taste

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大方 (via 萌典)

大概.etymology: Compound noun, adjective, and epistemic adverb of 大 ('general, broad') + 概 ('leveling stick for a grain measure -> general outline, approximate'): 'general idea/outline; roughly, probably, most likely'. Attested since Tang–Song prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大概 (via 萌典)

大白话.etymology: Three-character compound of 大 ('plain, thorough') + 白话 ('vernacular, plain unadorned speech', 白 'plain/unvarnished' + 话 'spoken words'): 'plain everyday speech, straightforward vernacular (as opposed to jargon or literary flourishes)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大白话 (via 萌典)

大街.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 大 ('main, wide') + 街 ('street, thoroughfare', 行 + 圭): 'main street, avenue, the street'.

history.stage: Tang–Song urban vernacular to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大街 (via 萌典)

大门.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 大 ('main, front') + 门 (門, 'gate, door'): 'main entrance, front gate, front door'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大门 (via 萌典)

大门口.etymology: Three-character locative compound of 大门 ('main gate, front door') + 口 ('entranceway, opening'): 'at the main entrance, right by the front gate/door'.

history.meaning: main doorway; by the front gate

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大门口 (via 萌典)

大雨.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 大 ('heavy, big') + 雨 ('rain'): 'heavy rain, downpour'. Attested from Shang oracle-bone weather divinations onward.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大雨 (via 萌典)

大雨倾盆.etymology: Four-character vivid idiom (also 倾盆大雨) combining 大雨 ('heavy rain') + 倾盆 ('overturn a basin of water', 倾 'tilt/pour out' + 盆 'basin'), describing rain pouring down in torrents as if emptied from an overturned basin.

history.stage: Tang–Song poetry (e.g., Du Fu, Su Shi) to Modern Mandarin
history.form: 大雨傾盆 / 大雨倾盆
history.meaning: rain pouring down as if from an upturned basin; torrential downpour

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 大雨倾盆 (via 萌典)

天.etymology: Ancient character attested on Shang oracle bones depicting a front-facing human figure (大) with the head or the vault above the head emphasized by a round or horizontal mark: 'the top of the head -> the sky, heaven, nature, day, weather, season'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Oracle bones & Classics) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: crown of the head -> sky, heaven, day, weather, nature

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 天 (via 萌典)

天亮.etymology: Subject-predicate compound of 天 ('the sky') + 亮 ('grow bright, become light'): 'daybreak, dawn, it gets light'.

history.meaning: the sky grows light = dawn, daybreak

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 天亮 (via 萌典)

天哪.etymology: Exclamatory phrase combining 天 ('Heaven!, the heavens') + emphatic modal particle 哪 (assimilation of 啊 after final -n of tiān): 'Good heavens!, Oh my God!, My goodness!'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 天哪 (via 萌典)

天气.etymology: Compound noun of 天 ('sky, heaven') + 气 (氣, 'vapor, breath, atmosphere'): in Classical Chinese 'the vital breath/ether of heaven' or 'time of day', and in modern Mandarin the standard word for 'weather'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 天气 (via 萌典)

天气预报.etymology: Four-character compound of 天气 ('weather', literally 'sky breath/atmosphere') + 预报 ('advance report', 预 'beforehand' + 报 'report/announce').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 天气预报

天生.etymology: Subject-predicate/adverb-verb compound used as an adjective and adverb, combining 天 ('Heaven, nature') + 生 ('give birth to, produce, born'): 'born with, innate, by nature, natural'. Famously in Li Bai's 天生我材必有用 ('Heaven made my talents for a purpose').

history.stage: Classical & Tang poetry to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 天生 (via 萌典)

天空.etymology: Compound noun of 天 ('sky, heaven') + 空 ('open space, vault of the air'): 'the sky, the firmament'.

history.stage: Medieval Buddhist & poetic Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 天空 (via 萌典)

天花板.etymology: Everyday word for 'ceiling', built from 天花 ('heavenly flowers') + 板 ('board'). 天花 first meant flowers falling from heaven in translated Buddhist texts; it was later applied to the decorated, painted panel ceilings of halls, and Ming–Qing builders called the grid of wooden panels 天花板. Modern Mandarin also uses it figuratively for an upper limit.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 天花板 (via 萌典)

太.etymology: Indicative character differentiated from 大 ('big, great') by adding a bottom dot (丶): originally interchangeable with 大 and 泰 ('supreme, extreme, highest'), and in Mandarin the primary degree adverb for 'too (excessively), extremely, so very (太好了!)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 太 (via 萌典)

太阳.etymology: Everyday spoken word for 'the sun': 太 ('great, utmost') + 阳 ('yang', the bright, warm principle opposed to 阴 yin). It is probably so named because the sun was seen as the utmost expression of yang. Classical Chinese usually said simply 日, which survives in words such as 日出 ('sunrise').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 太阳 (via 萌典)

夫妻.etymology: Coordinative kinship compound pairing 夫 ('husband, adult man', showing a man 大 with a hairpin 一 through his topknot marking adulthood) + 妻 ('wife', showing a woman 女 with hair held by a hand 又, denoting an equal partner in marriage): 'husband and wife, married couple'.

history.stage: Old Chinese (Shijing, Classics) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 夫妻 (via 萌典)

失物处.etymology: Three-character institutional compound combining 失物 ('lost property, lost items', 失 'lose' + 物 'object') + 处 (處, 'office, counter, department'): 'Lost and Found office/desk (short for 失物招领处)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 失物处 (via 萌典)

失误.etymology: Coordinative verb and noun compound of 失 ('lose, slip up, miss') + 误 (誤, 'err, mistake'): 'make a mistake, slip up, lapse, fault, error'. Attested since Han historical texts.

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 失误 (via 萌典)

失陪.etymology: Polite conversational formula combining 失 ('fail in, lose the chance to') + 陪 ('keep someone company'): literally 'fail to keep you company' -> 'excuse me for leaving first, I must be excusing myself'.

history.stage: Ming–Qing polite vernacular to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: excuse me for leaving your company

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 失陪 (via 萌典)

头上.etymology: Locative compound combining 头 (頭, 'head; top') + 上 ('on, above'): 'on one's head, overhead, on top'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 头上 (via 萌典)

头疼.etymology: Subject-predicate compound of 头 (頭, 'head') + 疼 ('ache, hurt'): literally 'have a headache' and figuratively 'find something a headache, feel troubled or exasperated by'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 头疼 (via 萌典)

夸.etymology: Phono-semantic character (traditional 誇, combining 言 'speech' + 夸 kuā 'spread wide, big'; simplified back to the base character 夸): originally 'speak big, boast, exaggerate' in Classical Chinese, and in everyday Mandarin 'praise, compliment, commend'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 夸 (via 萌典)

夸夸.etymology: Reduplicated verb from 夸 ('praise, compliment'): 'praise a bit, give someone a compliment' (distinguished in tone and syntax from the literary bound root 夸夸 kuākuā in 夸夸其谈 'boastful talk').

history.meaning: give a compliment; praise a little

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 夸夸 (via 萌典)

夹.etymology: Ancient ideogram (夾) attested on Shang oracle bones showing a central standing person (大) flanked under both arms by two smaller figures (二人): 'press from both sides, hold between, clip, pinch, carry under the arm, interleave' (read jiā), and 'double-layered/lined garment' (read jiá).

history.meaning: flank from both sides; press between; pincers/tongs

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 夹 (via 萌典)

奇怪.etymology: Coordinative adjective and verb compound of 奇 ('unusual, rare, strange') + 怪 ('strange, odd, marvel at'): 'strange, odd, surprising; find something strange'. Attested since Han–Six Dynasties prose and poetry.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 奇怪 (via 萌典)

女士.etymology: Compound of 女 ('woman, female') + 士 ('person of character/learning'). First attested in the Shijing (Book of Odes, 厘尔女士 'grant you a noble lady of virtue'), and standardized in modern Chinese as the polite formal title and noun for 'lady, Ms., madam, women (in public address)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 女士 (via 萌典)

奶白色.etymology: Three-character descriptive color compound combining 奶 ('milk') + 白色 ('white color'): 'milky white, cream white, off-white'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 奶白色 (via 萌典)

奶酪.etymology: Compound noun of 奶 ('milk') + 酪 ('fermented dairy curds/kumis/junket' in Classical and northern pastoral Chinese, 酉 'fermentation' + 各): standardized in modern Mandarin for 'cheese'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 奶酪 (via 萌典)

她.etymology: Third-person singular feminine pronoun ('she, her'), written with the woman component 女 beside 也 and pronounced tā identically to 他. Introduced into modern written Mandarin in the late 1910s (popularized by poet and linguist Liu Bannong) to distinguish 'she' visually on the page while preserving spoken tā.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 她 (via 萌典)

好.etymology: Core adjective 'good, fine, well' (hǎo), combining 女 ('woman') and 子 ('child'). Already among the earliest graphs on Shang oracle bones and ubiquitous in the Classic of Poetry, 好 expresses quality, readiness (修好了 'fixed and ready'), and greetings (你好 'hello').

history.meaning: good; fine; lovely (hǎo); to be fond of (hào)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好 (via 萌典)

好像.etymology: Compound adverb and verb of 好 ('quite, very', an intensifying adverb) + 像 ('resemble, be like'): 'seem, look like, as if'. Attested from Tang–Song poetry and vernacular.

history.meaning: very much resemble -> seem, look as if

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好像 (via 萌典)
