好吃.etymology: Evaluative compound adjective combining 好 ('good to…, pleasant to…', read hǎo) + 吃 ('eat'): 'good to eat -> delicious, tasty'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好吃 (via 萌典)

好听.etymology: Evaluative compound adjective combining 好 ('pleasant to…') + 听 (聽, 'listen to, hear'): 'pleasant to listen to -> nice-sounding, melodious, pleasing to the ear'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好听 (via 萌典)

好喝.etymology: Evaluative compound adjective combining 好 ('pleasant to…') + 喝 ('drink'): 'good to drink -> tasty, delicious (of beverages or soup)'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好喝 (via 萌典)

好在.etymology: Modal adverb and verb phrase combining 好 ('what is good/fortunate is…') + 在 ('lie in, consist in'): literally 'the good thing lies in…' -> 'fortunately, luckily, thank goodness that'.

history.meaning: the good thing is that -> fortunately, luckily

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好在 (via 萌典)

好奇.etymology: Verb-object compound used as an adjective, combining 好 (here read hào in the fourth tone, the Classical verb meaning 'be fond of, love') + 奇 ('novelty, strange or unfamiliar things'): 'curious, inquisitive'. Attested since Han historical prose (e.g., Sima Qian's Shiji).

history.stage: Han Classical Chinese (Shiji, Hanshu) to Modern Mandarin
history.meaning: fond of the novel/unusual -> curious, inquisitive

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好奇 (via 萌典)

好好.etymology: Reduplication of 好 ('good, well', read hǎohǎo or hǎohāor in northern speech): functions as an adverb meaning 'properly, carefully, thoroughly, to one's heart's content' (好好休息 'get a good rest') and as an adjective meaning 'perfectly fine, in good condition'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好好 (via 萌典)

好看.etymology: Evaluative compound adjective combining 好 ('pleasant to…') + 看 ('look at, watch'): 'pleasing to the eye -> good-looking, pretty, attractive; interesting (of a book, play, or film)'.

history.meaning: pleasing to look at; pretty; good-looking; interesting

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好看 (via 萌典)

好让.etymology: Purposive conjunction combining modal/purposive 好 ('so as to, so that it is easy to…') + causative verb 让 (讓, 'let, allow'): 'so as to let, in order that'.

history.meaning: so as to let; so that

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好让 (via 萌典)

好运.etymology: Modifier-head compound noun of 好 ('good') + 运 (運, 'revolving fortune, luck'): 'good luck, good fortune'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 好运 (via 萌典)

如果.etymology: Conditional conjunction combining two Classical conditional markers: 如 ('if, suppose') + 果 ('if indeed, really, as expected'): 'if, in case, supposing that'. Attested from Tang–Song poetry and prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 如果 (via 萌典)

妈妈.etymology: Intimate reduplication of 妈 (woman classifier 女 + phonetic 马 mǎ), part of the near-universal bilabial nasal nursery pattern for 'mother' while anchored in Chinese script since the Guangyun dictionary (Middle Chinese).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 妈妈 (via 萌典)

妙.etymology: Ideographic/phono-semantic character combining 女 ('woman/maiden') + 少 ('young/subtle', also written 玅 with 玄 'mysterious'): in Classical Chinese (Laozi's 众妙之门) 'subtle, mysterious, wondrous', and in everyday Mandarin 'wonderful, clever, ingenious, fine'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 妙 (via 萌典)

姑姑.etymology: Affectionate kinship reduplication of 姑 (woman classifier 女 + phonetic 古 gǔ), attested since the Erya and Book of Odes specifically for one's father's sister—reflecting Chinese kinship's precise distinction between paternal (姑姑) and maternal (姨妈/阿姨) aunts.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 姑姑 (via 萌典)

姑娘.etymology: Compound noun combining 姑 ('father's sister; young unmarried woman') + 娘 ('mother; young woman', neutral tone niang in this word): 'unmarried young woman, girl; daughter; (historically) paternal aunt'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 姑娘 (via 萌典)

姓.etymology: Ancient ideogram/phono-semantic character attested on Shang oracle bones combining 女 ('woman') + 生 ('be born, give birth'): originally denoted a matriarchal clan lineage name shared by those born of the same ancestral mother (such as the ancient 姬, 姜, 嬴, 姒 clan names containing 女), now the general noun and verb for 'family name, surname; be surnamed'.

history.meaning: born of the same clan mother = ancestral clan surname

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 姓 (via 萌典)

嫩.etymology: Phono-semantic character of 女 ('delicate') + 敕 (shù/nèn): 'tender, soft, delicate (of young shoots, meat, or skin); inexperienced; light/pale (of colors)'.

history.stage: Classical & Medieval Chinese to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 嫩 (via 萌典)

字.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on bronze vessels showing a child (子) under a house roof (宀): originally 'give birth to, rear and nurture a child' (and 'a woman's betrothal', 待字闺中). Because characters proliferated by compounding radicals and phonetics like offspring, since the Qin dynasty 字 has meant 'written Chinese character, word, script, handwriting' (as well as an adult courtesy name).

history.meaning: child under a roof = bear/rear offspring; adult courtesy name

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 字 (via 萌典)

字母.etymology: Compound noun of 字 ('written word/character') + 母 ('mother, generative root'). Originally coined by Tang–Song Chinese phonologists (after Buddhist Sanskrit models) for the 36 initial consonant exemplars (三十六字母) from which syllables were generated, and adopted in modern Mandarin for an 'alphabetic letter, alphabet'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 字母 (via 萌典)

字迹.etymology: Compound noun of 字 ('written characters') + 迹 (跡, 'footprints, traces, marks'): 'handwriting, written characters/script left on a surface'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 字迹 (via 萌典)

孙子.etymology: Kinship noun formed from 孙 (孫, combining 子 'child' + 系 'thread of descent/continuation': 'child's child, descendant') + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'grandson (specifically son's son)' (contrast классический 孫子 Sūnzǐ with full third tone on 子, 'Master Sun', author of The Art of War).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 孙子 (via 萌典)

学校.etymology: Coordinative noun compound pairing two ancient Zhou-era educational institutions mentioned in Mencius (设痒序学校以教之): 学 (學, 'institution of higher learning; study') + 校 (xiào, 'community school and military training enclosure'). Standardized across modern East Asia for any 'school, educational institution'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 学校 (via 萌典)

孩子.etymology: Compound noun of 孩 ('laughing infant, young child', from 子 'child' + phonetic 亥 hài, originally 咳 'infant's giggle' in Laozi and Mencius) + nominal suffix 子 (neutral tone zi): 'child, kid; one's son or daughter'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 孩子 (via 萌典)

宁静.etymology: Coordinative adjective compound of 宁 (寧, 'peaceful, settled at heart under a roof with a dish of food') + 静 (靜, 'quiet, still, calm'): 'peaceful and quiet, tranquil, serene'. Famously in Zhuge Liang's 夫君子之行，静以修身…非淡泊无以明志，非宁静无以致远.

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Chuci, Huainanzi, Zhuge Liang) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 宁静 (via 萌典)

它.etymology: Non-human third-person singular pronoun ('it'). In Shang oracle-bone script, 它 was the original pictograph of a cobra/snake (written 蛇 shé after the insect/reptile radical 虫 was added), borrowed in Classical Chinese to mean 'other, another' (later written 他 with 亻). During the early 20th-century vernacular movement, 它 (alongside 牠 for animals) was standardized with the pronunciation tā for inanimate 'it', contrasting graphically with 他 ('he') and 她 ('she').

morphemes.meaning: classical 'other' standardized in modern Chinese for inanimate 'it' (tā)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 它 (via 萌典)

它们.etymology: Non-human third-person plural pronoun ('they, them [for things, plants, and animals]'), formed by adding the plural suffix 们 (-men) to the inanimate pronoun 它 ('it').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 它们 (via 萌典)

守.etymology: Ancient ideogram attested on bronze inscriptions combining 宀 ('roof, building, court') + 寸 ('hand; law/measure'): 'guard, defend, keep watch over, abide by (rules/promises), stay close by'.

history.meaning: guard a territory/post; abide by; keep
guard; defend; observe/abide by; stay close to

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 守 (via 萌典)

安全.etymology: Coordinative adjective and noun compound of 安 ('peaceful, settled, safe', a woman 女 settled indoors under a roof 宀) + 全 ('whole, intact, unharmed'): 'safe and sound, secure; safety, security'. Attested since Classical prose (Xunzi, Hanshu).

history.stage: Classical Chinese (Xunzi, Hanshu) to Modern Mandarin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 安全 (via 萌典)

客栈.etymology: Traditional courtyard inn or boutique guesthouse (counted with 家: 一家客栈), combining 客 ('traveler, guest') with 栈 ('wooden gallery, storehouse, wayside lodge'). Historic 客棧 served merchants and travelers along imperial post roads and remain iconic in preserved old quarters of Chengdu and Southwest China.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 客棧 (via 萌典)

对不起.etymology: Sincere everyday apology ('I'm sorry'), a potential-complement phrase literally meaning 'unable to face (you) squarely / let you down': 对 ('face, treat rightly') + 不 ('not') + 起 ('measure up'). Standardized in Qing and modern Mandarin alongside its classic reassuring reply 没关系 ('it doesn't matter').

history.meaning: have let someone down; 'I am sorry'

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 對不起 (via 萌典)

常春藤.etymology: Botanical compound of 常 ('ever, constant') + 春 ('springtime greenness') + 藤 ('climbing vine', grass/plant crown 艹 + 滕), literally 'ever-spring vine' because its leaves stay glossy green through winter.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 常春藤

开关.etymology: Antonymic verb-pair compound turned noun: 开 ('open / switch on', originally two hands lifting a bar from门 gate leaves) + 关 ('shut / switch off', a crossbar latching门 shut). By pairing opposite actions, 开关 names an electrical switch or valve.

history.meaning: opening and closing a gate or pass

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 开关 (via 萌典)

张.etymology: Measure word for flat, spread-out surfaces and paper items (一张桌子 'a table', 一张纸 'a sheet of paper', 一张床 'a bed'). Formed from 弓 ('bow') + 长 (cháng phonetic), 張 originally meant 'string and draw a bow open' in the Shijing, extending naturally to things spread flat.

history.meaning: classifier for flat sheets, tables, beds

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 張 (via 萌典)

很.etymology: Degree adverb ('very') that also serves as the natural, unstressed link before simple predicate adjectives (今天很冷 'It is cold today'). In Classical Chinese (Shuo Wen Jie Zi, Zhanguo Ce), 很 meant 'unyielding, intractable, severe'; in Ming–Qing colloquial Mandarin that intensity bleached into the everyday degree word 'very'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 很 (via 萌典)

怎么.etymology: Interrogative adverb asking 'how?' or 'how come?' directly before a verb (怎么走？ 'how do I get there?', 怎么拿错了？ 'how did it get mixed up?'). Formed with the same colloquial -么 suffix as 什么 and attested throughout Ming–Qing vernacular fiction.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 怎麼 (via 萌典)

您.etymology: Polite singular second-person pronoun ('you'), formed by placing 你 ('you') above 心 ('heart') to signal respectful deference. Emerging in Jin and Yuan dynasty northern vernacular (originally fused from plural 你们 in polite address), 您 became Standard Mandarin's courteous pronoun for elders, teachers, and guests.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 您 (via 萌典)

您好.etymology: Polite Mandarin greeting ('hello'), substituting respectful 您 ('you') for everyday 你 before 好 ('well'). Used when greeting guests at a front desk, teachers, or elders.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 您好 (via 萌典)

想.etymology: Mental and modal verb meaning 'think of, miss, would like to', combining 相 ('observe, mutual appearance', phonetic xiāng) above 心 ('heart-mind'). Attested in Han-dynasty texts for calling an image to mind, 想 before another verb expresses a polite wish ('would like to') softer than direct 要.

history.meaning: call to mind; long for; think

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 想 (via 萌典)

我.etymology: First-person singular pronoun ('I, me'), attested since Late Shang oracle-bone inscriptions, where the graph depicted a notched polearm before being borrowed phonetically for the first-person pronoun. In Classical Chinese texts such as the Classic of Poetry (Shijing) and Analects, 我 already serves unchanged as both subject 'I' and object 'me'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 我 (via 萌典)

我们.etymology: First-person plural pronoun ('we, us'), combining 我 ('I') with the human plural suffix 们 (men). Plural markers written 弭, 伟, 懣, and finally 們 appear in Song and Yuan vernacular literature to form collective personal pronouns.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 我們 (via 萌典)

房间.etymology: Everyday two-syllable noun for 'room' (counted with 间: 一间房间), pairing 房 ('side house, chamber', attested in the Shijing) with 间 ('architectural bay, room space').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 房間 (via 萌典)

扁豆.etymology: Descriptive botanical compound of 扁 ('flat, compressed') + 豆 ('bean, legume', originally a pictograph of a footed food vessel in oracle-bone script, transferred to pulses served in it), naming flat-seeded lentils and hyacinth beans.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 扁豆

把.etymology: Measure word for objects you grip by a handle or back (一把钥匙 'a key', 一把椅子 'a chair') AND disposal coverb fronting a definite object before an action verb (把门打开). Both functions grew directly out of the Classical Chinese verb 把 ('grasp, hold in the hand', combining 扌 'hand' + 巴 phonetic).

history.meaning: hold or grasp in the hand
classifier for handled items; object-fronting marker

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 把 (via 萌典)

折扣.etymology: Merchant accounting compound of 折 ('break off, reduce proportionally') + 扣 ('hold back, deduct from a sum'). In Chinese shopkeeper usage, 打九折 states the fraction retained (9/10 = 90%), whereas 折扣 names the price reduction itself.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 折扣 (via 萌典)

报纸.etymology: Compound of 报 ('report, gazette, bulletin', as in imperial 邸报 court gazettes) + 纸 ('paper', silk/fibre radical 纟 + 氏, perfected during the Eastern Han).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 报纸 (via 萌典)

拱门.etymology: Compound of 拱 ('join hands in a curved bow; arch', hand classifier 扌 + phonetic 共 gǒng) + 门 ('gate, doorway', pictograph of double swinging gate leaves), naming a curved stone or brick archway.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 拱门 (via 萌典)

旋律.etymology: Sino-Japanese / literary Chinese musical compound combining 旋 ('revolve, return in phrases') + 律 ('pitch-pipe standard, musical law/temperament'). Standardized across modern East Asian musical terminology to render 'melody'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 旋律 (via 萌典)

早上.etymology: Everyday noun for 'morning' (early morning until around nine or ten o'clock), combining 早 ('early, dawn', attested throughout Classical Chinese) with the noun-forming time/location suffix 上. Pairs with 好 to form the warm greeting 早上好！ ('Good morning!').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 早上 (via 萌典)

明天.etymology: Noun meaning 'tomorrow', combining 明 ('bright, next dawning', combining 日 'sun' + 月 'moon') with 天 ('day, sky'). Classical Chinese said 明日 ('next sun/day'); vernacular Mandarin replaced 日 with everyday 天 to form 明天.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 明天 (via 萌典)

是.etymology: Equative copula ('be: am, is, are') linking two nouns or noun phrases. In Classical Chinese (Analects, Mencius), 是 originally functioned as the proximal demonstrative 'this' and adjective 'right, correct'; in Han-dynasty prose its résumé position between topic and predicate ('X, this [is] Y') reanalyzed into the modern copula 'be'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 是 (via 萌典)

有.etymology: Verb of possession ('have') and existence ('there is, there are'), attested from Shang oracle bones and bronze inscriptions through Classical and modern Mandarin. Unlike every other Mandarin verb, 有 is always negated with 没 (没有), never 不.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 有 (via 萌典)

本.etymology: Measure word for bound books, notebooks, and ledgers (一本书 'a book', 一本账本 'a ledger'). Formed by marking the lower root of 木 ('tree') with a stroke, 本 meant 'tree root, foundation, origin' in Classical Chinese, then 'bound volume' once bamboo slips were superseded by stitched codices.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 本 (via 萌典)

杏仁.etymology: Compound of 杏 ('apricot/almond tree', wood 木 + 口) + 仁 ('edible seed kernel inside a pit', extended from 'humane heart/core' to the tender inner seed of stone fruits); used in Chinese baking and herbal cuisine for sweet almonds and apricot kernels.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 杏仁

条.etymology: Measure word for long, narrow, or winding things: streets, lanes, rivers, towels, trousers, and legal clauses (一条老街 'an old street', 一条毛巾 'a towel'). In the Classic of Poetry, 條 originally named a long, slender tree branch, from which the long-strip classifier grew.

history.meaning: classifier for streets, rivers, ropes, clauses

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 條 (via 萌典)

杯.etymology: Noun 'cup' and measure word for cupfuls or glassfuls of drinks (一杯热茶 'a cup of hot tea', 一杯咖啡 'a cup of coffee'). Written with 木 ('wood', reflecting early lacquered wooden drinking vessels) and 不 phonetic, 杯 is attested in Classical banqueting scenes in the Shiji and Mencius.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 杯 (via 萌典)

杯子.etymology: Formed from 杯 ('cup', phono-semantic character with 木 'wood'—reflecting early lacquered wooden drinking vessels—and phonetic 不) plus the nominalizing diminutive suffix 子 (neutral tone zi), which turns monosyllabic nouns into natural two-syllable spoken Mandarin words.

history.meaning: lacquered wooden or ceramic wine/soup cup

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 杯子 (via 萌典)

柠檬.etymology: Disyllabic phonetic loan for 'lemon' written with two tree-radical characters (木 + 宁 níng and 木 + 蒙 méng). Attested in Song–Yuan maritime and botanical records (such as Fan Chengda's Guihai Yuheng Zhi and southern trade glossaries) transcribing Indo-Iranian / Malay-Arabic citrus terms ultimately akin to Sanskrit nimbū and Persian līmūn.

morphemes.kind: phonetic loan syllable (with 木 tree radical)
phonetic loan syllable (with 木 tree radical)

history.meaning: tart citrus fruit cultivated in Lingnan

cognates.meaning: citrus fruit borrowed along the same Indo-Persian trade network

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 柠檬 (via 萌典)

梯子.etymology: Derived from 梯 ('wooden steps or ladder', wood radical 木 + phonetic 弟 dì, which also carries the sense 'ordered sequence/steps') + nominal suffix 子 (-zi).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 梯子

椅子.etymology: Formed from 椅 (wood radical 木 + phonetic 奇 qí; originally a type of catalpa tree in Classical texts, reassigned during the Tang–Song transition from floor mats to high-seated backed chairs) + nominal suffix 子.

history.meaning: folding chair and backed wooden chair

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 椅子 (via 萌典)

橄榄油.etymology: Compound of 橄榄 ('olive', originally naming native Chinese Canarium white/black olives with wood radical 木 on both characters, then applied to Mediterranean Olea europaea) + 油 ('pressed oil').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 橄榄油

水.etymology: Fundamental noun 'water' (shuǐ), descended from an oracle-bone pictograph of a flowing stream flanked by ripples and droplets. Serves both as an independent word (热水 'hot water', 喝水 'drink water') and as the left-hand component 氵 in hundreds of liquid-related characters.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 水 (via 萌典)

水桶.etymology: Compound of 水 ('water') + 桶 ('staved wooden pail or tub', wood radical 木 + phonetic 甬 yǒng), preserved even when modern buckets are metal or plastic.

history.meaning: coopered wooden measure or water bucket

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 水桶

没.etymology: Existential and past-completion negator read méi ('not have; did not'), written with the water component 氵. Under its literary reading mò ('sink, submerge'), the graph appears in Classical Chinese; by late Tang and Song lyric poetry (such as Wei Zhuang's ci), 沒 had grammaticalized in spoken Chinese to negate 有 and completed events.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 沒 (via 萌典)

没关系.etymology: Warm reassuring reply to an apology ('it doesn't matter; no problem'), combining 没 ('not have') with 关系 ('connection, bearing, consequence'—literally 'no bearing / nothing to worry over').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 沒關係 (via 萌典)

没有.etymology: Negative counterpart of 有 ('do not have; there is no; did not'), combining the negative 没 with 有. Established in Song–Yuan vernacular texts, 没有 both negates possession/existence before nouns and negates completed actions before verbs.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 沒有 (via 萌典)

油漆.etymology: Coordinate craft compound of 油 ('drying tung oil', pressed from Aleurites fordii seeds to waterproof timber) + 漆 ('natural lacquer sap' from Toxicodendron vernicifluum trees, attested since Neolithic China); together naming protective architectural paint.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 油漆

海绵.etymology: Compound of 海 ('sea') + 绵 ('soft silk floss', silk radical 纟 + 帛 'fine cloth'), originally describing natural marine sponges by likening their porous springiness to silk wadding, later extended to synthetic cleaning sponges.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 海绵

照片.etymology: Word for 'photo', built from 照 ('shine on, reflect; take a picture', as in 照相 'take a photo') + 片 ('thin flat piece, card'). The second character names the flat print, just as in 名片 ('business card') and 明信片 ('postcard'). A near synonym is 相片.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 照片 (via 萌典)

现金.etymology: Compound of 现 ('present, on hand, ready', jade radical 王 + 见 'visible right now') + 金 ('metal, gold, money'), literally 'ready money in hand' as opposed to credit or account transfers.

history.meaning: ready silver or cash on the spot

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 现金 (via 萌典)

玻璃.etymology: Ancient Buddhist / Silk Road loanword attested since Medieval Chinese (originally 颇黎 / 玻璃, transcribing Sanskrit sphaṭika 'rock crystal, quartz'), written with two jade-radical characters (王/玉) because clear blown glass and rock crystal were prized alongside translucent gems.

history.meaning: rock crystal or imported clear glass (from Sanskrit sphaṭika)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 玻璃 (via 萌典)

琴弦.etymology: Compound of 琴 ('stringed or keyboard instrument') + 弦 ('bowstring; taut musical string', bow radical 弓 +玄, attested since Pre-Qin classics for silk guqin strings and now steel piano strings).

history.meaning: silk strings of a seven-stringed qin zither
musical string; piano or violin string

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 琴弦

琴槌.etymology: Compound of 琴 ('piano; struck-string instrument') + 槌 ('wooden mallet or drumstick', wood radical 木 + phonetic 追 zhuī), naming the felt-covered wooden hammers inside an acoustic piano action.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 琴槌

琴键.etymology: Musical compound of 琴 ('zither; keyboard instrument', depicting two jade-like bridges 珏 over string resonance, generalized in modern Chinese to pianos and organs) + 键 ('metal bolt, latch pin, or lever key', metal radical 钅 + phonetic 建 jiàn).

history.meaning: metal door bolt or axle pin

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 琴键

电线.etymology: Modern compound combining 电 ('electricity', originally 'lightning' flashing under rain 雨 in oracle-bone and bronze script) + 线 ('thread, wire', silk radical 纟 + phonetic 戋).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 电线 (via 萌典)

番茄.etymology: Botanical naming compound of 番 ('foreign, introduced from overseas', originally referring to non-Han borderlands and maritime trade) + 茄 ('eggplant/nightshade fruit', plant radical 艹 + 加), literally 'foreign eggplant' after tomatoes arrived via maritime trade in the Ming dynasty.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 番茄

登记本.etymology: Compound of 登记 ('enter in a register', 登 'ascend/enter on an official roll' + 记 'write down/record') + 本 ('bound notebook or volume', originally a mark at the base of 木 'tree', extended via bamboo/paper bindings to books).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 登记本

的.etymology: Structural particle de linking an owner, noun, adjective, or clause to a following noun (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard'), or forming a headless possessive ('mine, Teacher Song's'). In Tang–Song vernacular texts this linker was often written 底 (dǐ) before standardizing on 的 in Yuan–Ming prose.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 的 (via 萌典)

砂纸.etymology: Compound of 砂 ('coarse mineral grit, quartz/emery sand', stone radical 石 + 少) + 纸 ('paper'), naming abrasive grit bonded onto heavy paper backing for carpentry smoothing.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 砂纸

硬币.etymology: Compound of 硬 ('hard, rigid', stone radical 石 + 更) + 币 ('currency', originally ritual silk offerings in Classical Chinese, later generalized to money), contrasting metal coins with paper 纸币.

history.meaning: ritual silk gift; medium of exchange

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 硬币 (via 萌典)

秋天.etymology: Compound of 秋 ('autumn, harvest', combining 禾 'ripening grain stalk' + 火 'fire', originally depicting harvest grain and hearth/field fire in oracle-bone script) + 天 ('season, sky').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 秋天 (via 萌典)

秘密.etymology: Word for 'secret', a compound of two near synonyms: 秘 ('hidden, secret'; variant 祕 with the spirit/altar component) and 密 ('dense, close, concealed'). 秘 was historically read bì and still has a b- initial in most other Chinese varieties; Mandarin mì comes from its conflation with 密 in this very compound.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 秘密 (via 萌典)

窗户.etymology: Coordinate architectural compound of 窗 ('window opening, lattice skylight', cave/roof opening radical 穴 + phonetic 囱 'chimney/vent') + 户 ('single-leaf casement or shuttered opening', pictograph of half a double gate 门). The neutral-tone second syllable marks lexicalized everyday Mandarin.

history.meaning: skylight lattice (窗) and casement door/shutter (户)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 窗户

篮子.etymology: Formed from 篮 ('handled basket', bamboo radical 竹 atop phonetic 监 jiān, reflecting woven split-bamboo craft) + everyday noun suffix 子.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 篮子 (via 萌典)

老板.etymology: Originally written 老版 in southern river-port and theatrical guilds (老 respectful prefix + 板/版 'wooden printing block, shop counter, or rhythmic clapper'), addressing the proprietor or master of an inn, workshop, or troupe; now standard relaxed Mandarin for 'boss' or 'shopkeeper'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 老板 (via 萌典)

肥皂.etymology: Compound of 肥 ('plump, rich, fatty') + 皂 ('black soap-pod cleanser', from 皂荚 Gleditsia sinensis pods traditionally boiled or pounded into washing cakes in China before tallow/oil bar soaps arrived).

history.meaning: plump soap-bean pods pounded into washing balls

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 肥皂

胶带.etymology: Descriptive compound of 胶 ('glue, gum, rubber', flesh/organic radical 月 + phonetic 交) + 带 ('belt, ribbon, strip', pictograph of a waist sash with hanging cloth).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 胶带 (via 萌典)

胶水.etymology: Compound of 胶 ('animal hide glue, plant resin, adhesive', flesh/organic radical 月 + phonetic 交 jiāo 'join together') + 水 ('liquid, water'), naming liquid glue in contrast to solid glue sticks or tape.

history.meaning: joinery glue used in bows, wheels, and instruments

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 胶水

节奏.etymology: Classical musical compound of 节 ('bamboo node; regular metrical division', bamboo radical 竹 + 即, because bamboo joints divide a stalk into measured intervals) + 奏 ('perform music, advance in time').

morphemes.meaning: bamboo joint; regular beat or measure

history.meaning: measured pauses and movement in music and ritual

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 节奏

花盆.etymology: Compound of 花 ('blossom, flower', grass/plant radical 艹 + phonetic 化) + 盆 ('basin, pot', phonetic 分 atop 皿 'vessel/dish').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 花盆 (via 萌典)

茶.etymology: Mandarin word for 'tea' (chá), written with 艹 ('plant'), 人, and 木 ('tree'). Prior to the Mid-Tang dynasty, tea was written with the shared bitter-herb graph 荼 (tú); tea master Lu Yu's Classic of Tea (Cha Jing, c. 760) popularized removing one horizontal stroke to establish 茶—the ancestor of English 'tea' (via Hokkien tê) and 'chai' (via northern chá).

history.stage: Tang dynasty (Lu Yu, Cha Jing, c. 760)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 茶 (via 萌典)

茶杯.etymology: Modifier-head compound of 茶 ('tea', graphically split from 荼 tú during the Tang dynasty around Lu Yu's Classic of Tea) + 杯 ('cup'), naming a vessel dedicated to hot tea.

history.form: 茶瓯 / 茶盏 / 茶杯

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 茶杯 (via 萌典)

菜单.etymology: Compound of 菜 ('cooked dish, vegetable/course', plant crown 艹 + 采 'pluck/gather') + 单 ('single sheet, itemized list'), naming a written restaurant or café bill of fare.

history.meaning: written list of dishes for a banquet or tavern

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 菜单

薄荷茶.etymology: Compound of 薄荷 ('mint, Mentha', plant crown 艹 on both characters; note colloquial reading bò he preserving an older disyllabic herbal name) + 茶 ('tea, herbal infusion').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 薄荷茶

蜂蜜.etymology: Transparent compound of 蜂 ('bee', combining the insect classifier 虫 with phonetic 夆 fēng) + 蜜 ('honey', combining 虫 at the base with phonetic 宓 mì). Notably, Old Chinese *mit (蜜) is widely recognized as an ancient Silk Road / Central Asian loanword cognate with Tocharian B mit ('honey, mead') and Proto-Indo-European *médʰu.

rootFamily.gloss: hundred flowers (as in 百花蜂蜜)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 蜂蜜 (via 萌典)

螺丝.etymology: Compound of 螺 ('spiral snail/conch shell', insect/mollusc classifier 虫 + 累) + 丝 ('fine thread'), vividly likening the helical threading on a metal screw to the spiral whorls of a snail shell.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 螺丝 (via 萌典)

要.etymology: High-frequency verb and modal ('want, need, will / be going to'). Originally depicting two hands at the waist (later clarified as 腰 'waist'), 要 in Classical Chinese meant 'seek, invite, essential' (yāo / yào), from which vernacular Mandarin developed 'need, want' and imminent future 'be about to'.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 要 (via 萌典)

请.etymology: Polite request marker ('please') and hospitality verb ('invite; treat someone to a meal'), combining 讠 ('words') with 青 (qīng phonetic). In Classical Chinese etiquette (Analects, Liji), 請 meant 'respectfully request permission or invite', which remains the heart of modern 请进 ('please come in') and 请坐 ('please sit').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 請 (via 萌典)

请问.etymology: Polite question opener ('excuse me, may I ask…'), pairing 请 ('respectfully request') with 问 ('ask'). Already attested as a courteous formula in Classical dialogues in Mencius ('Dare I respectfully ask…'), it remains Standard Mandarin's everyday way to approach a front desk or stranger.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 請問 (via 萌典)

谁.etymology: Interrogative pronoun 'who, whom' (shuí or shéi), combining 言/讠 ('speech, ask') with 隹 (zhuī phonetic). Already standard across Classical Chinese (Shijing, Analects), 谁 stays in place in Mandarin questions and takes 的 to form 谁的 ('whose?').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 誰 (via 萌典)

谢谢.etymology: Everyday expression of gratitude ('thank you'), formed by reduplicating 谢 ('thank, express gratitude; decline politely', written with 讠 'speech' + 射 phonetic). Single 謝 for thanking someone appears in Han-dynasty historical records (Shiji), while reduplicated 謝謝 became standard in Ming–Qing spoken Mandarin.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 謝謝 (via 萌典)

这.etymology: Proximal demonstrative ('this'), pairing with a measure word before nouns (这个 'this one', 这间房 'this room'). Written with the movement component 辶 plus 言, 這 emerged in Tang–Song vernacular Chinese (alongside earlier 者) to replace Classical 此 ('this').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 這 (via 萌典)

这里.etymology: Location pronoun meaning 'here' ('this place'), formed strictly parallel to 那里 ('there') and 哪里 ('where'). Placed right after 在 to anchor where someone or something is.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 這裡 (via 萌典)

那.etymology: Distal demonstrative ('that'), pairing with a measure word before nouns (那个 'that one', 那条街 'that street') or opening a clause with 'well then'. Attested as a demonstrative in Han–Six Dynasties colloquial texts, contrasting directly with proximal 这.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 那 (via 萌典)

醋.etymology: Originally borrowed from a homophonous Classical graph meaning 'guest toasting the host' (wine/fermentation radical 酉 + phonetic 昔 xī), adopted to replace the older Classical word 酢/醯 ('sour fermented grain vinegar') so host-and-guest ritual toasts would not be confused with sourness.

钢琴.etymology: Modern descriptive compound coined in late Qing / early Republican China from 钢 ('steel', 金 metal + 冈 phonetic) + 琴 ('zither / stringed instrument', depicting jade-bridged strings), highlighting the steel wire strings inside a Western piano in contrast to silk-stringed classical 琴.

morphemes.meaning: steel (referring to steel strings and frame)

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 钢琴 (via 萌典)

钥匙.etymology: Compound noun 'key' (yào shi, counted with 把: 一把钥匙), combining two metal-radical (钅/金) words: 钥 ('lock bolt / key') and 匙 ('key / spoon'). In Classical texts 鑰 named the metal bolt of a gate lock while 匙 named the key inserted to open it; vernacular Mandarin joined the pair into one disyllabic noun.

history.meaning: lock bolt + key -> compound 鑰匙 'key'

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 鑰匙 (via 萌典)

铅笔.etymology: Compound of 铅 ('lead', metal radical 钅 + 铅) + 笔 ('writing brush/pen', bamboo radical 竹 + 毛 'hair', from traditional bamboo-shafted ink brushes). Like English 'lead pencil', 铅笔 preserves the historical misnomer equating dark graphite cores with metallic lead.

history.meaning: white-lead cosmetic or correction stylus for manuscripts

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 铅笔 (via 萌典)

镊子.etymology: Derived from 镊 ('pinch or pluck with small metal tongs', metal radical 钅 + phonetic 聂 niè) + nominal suffix 子 (-zi), attested since medical and goldsmithing treatises for fine precision tweezers.

history.meaning: small metal pincers; hair or splinter tweezers

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 镊子

门.etymology: Core noun 'door, gate', descended directly from a Shang oracle-bone pictograph of two swinging wooden gate leaves under a lintel. Counted with the measure word 扇 (一扇门 'a door') and productive in compounds like 开门 ('open the door'), 门口 ('doorway'), and 大门 ('front gate').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 門 (via 萌典)

闪电.etymology: Compound of 闪 ('flash, dart suddenly', pictograph of a person 人 dodging swiftly through a doorway 门) + 电 ('lightning', rain cloud 雨 above a jagged flash 申 in bronze/oracle script, before 电 was extended to modern electricity).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 闪电

间.etymology: Measure word for rooms of every kind (一间客房 'a guest room', 一间书房 'a study'), combining 门 ('doorway, gate') with 日 ('sunlight'). Depicting light peeking through a doorway gap, 間 in Classical Chinese meant 'interval, space between' and the bay between building pillars—hence one room.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 間 (via 萌典)

阁楼.etymology: Architectural compound of 阁 ('elevated timber pavilion or upper chamber', gate radical 门 + phonetic 各 gè) + 楼 ('multi-storey timber building', wood radical 木 + phonetic 娄 lóu), naming a tucked upper loft or attic beneath a pitched roof.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 阁楼

陶瓷.etymology: Coordinative compound uniting China's two great fired-clay traditions: 陶 ('earthenware/stoneware', combining 阝 mound with 匋 depicting a kiln wrapping fired vessels) and 瓷 ('high-fired glazed porcelain', combining phonetic 次 cì with 瓦 'tile/ceramic ware').

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 陶瓷 (via 萌典)

集市.etymology: Compound of 集 ('gather together', originally depicting birds 隹 perched together on a tree 木) + 市 ('market', attested from bronze inscriptions for a walled trading precinct). Together 集市 names a periodic or open-air neighbourhood market where farmers and craftspeople gather.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 集市 (via 萌典)

需要.etymology: Compound verb and noun meaning 'need, require', pairing 需 ('await, require', attested in the Yijing) with 要 ('essential, need'). Used in polite requests and everyday explanations of what a task calls for.

history.stage: Classical roots in Yijing (需) & Mencius (要)
history.meaning: require + essential -> modern compound 需要 'need'

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 需要 (via 萌典)

音乐.etymology: Word for 'music', joining 音 ('sound, tone') and 乐 (yuè, 'music'; the same character read lè means 'joy'). The compound 音樂 is attested in Classical Chinese for musical sound and ritual music; in the late 19th century it was standardized (in Japanese 音楽 ongaku as well) as the general term for music as an art, and that modern sense became standard in Chinese.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 音乐 (via 萌典)

预算.etymology: Compound of 预 ('beforehand, in advance') + 算 ('calculate with counting rods', bamboo 竹 + 具 + 廾 two hands).

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 预算 (via 萌典)

饼干.etymology: Compound of 饼 ('flat round grain cake or pastry', food radical 饣 + phonetic 并 bìng) + 干 (gān, 'baked dry, moisture-free'), originally naming dry travel rations and adopted in modern Mandarin for crisp biscuits and cookies.

sources.title: MOE Revised Mandarin Dictionary — 饼干

黄铜.etymology: Metallurgical compound of 黄 ('yellow, golden') + 铜 ('copper', metal radical 钅 + phonetic 同 tóng), distinguishing yellow copper-zinc brass from reddish pure copper (红铜/紫铜) and tin bronze (青铜).
